name: Education
blurb: Trường lớp, phương pháp học, bằng cấp

words.definitionEn: relating to education, especially at a college or university level
words.example: Students must maintain a high academic standard to qualify for the scholarship.

words.definitionEn: official approval given by an authority, usually to an educational institution or program
words.example: The university lost its accreditation after failing to meet the required standards.

words.definitionEn: graduates or former students of a particular school, college, or university
words.example: Many alumni donate generously to support scholarships for current students.

words.definitionEn: a system of training a new generation of practitioners in a trade or profession with on-the-job training and often some accompanying study
words.example: She decided to pursue an apprenticeship rather than a traditional university degree.

words.definitionEn: the evaluation or estimation of the nature, quality, or ability of someone or something
words.example: Continuous assessment is used to monitor students' progress throughout the semester.

words.definitionEn: an academic degree or qualification, especially the International Baccalaureate or a bachelor's degree
words.example: The International Baccalaureate program is recognized by universities worldwide.

words.definitionEn: a ceremony at which students receive their academic degrees or diplomas
words.example: The commencement speech was delivered by a renowned alumnus.

words.definitionEn: required by law or a rule; obligatory
words.example: In many countries, education is compulsory for children between the ages of 6 and 16.

words.definitionEn: covering a wide range of topics or details; thorough
words.example: A comprehensive curriculum includes both theoretical knowledge and practical skills.

words.definitionEn: a qualification, achievement, or quality that gives someone a basis for trust or authority
words.example: Employers often require candidates to present their academic credentials.

words.definitionEn: the subjects comprising a course of study in a school or college
words.example: The school is revising its curriculum to include more digital literacy.

words.definitionEn: a written overview of a person's education, qualifications, and experience
words.example: Applicants are requested to submit a detailed curriculum vitae with their application.

words.definitionEn: the head of a faculty or department in a college or university
words.example: The dean of the faculty of engineering announced a new research initiative.

words.definitionEn: a qualification awarded by a college or university after completing a course of study
words.example: She earned a degree in economics from a prestigious university.

words.definitionEn: intended to teach, especially in a way that is morally instructive
words.example: The didactic approach of the lecture left little room for student interaction.

words.definitionEn: a certificate awarded by an educational institution for completing a course of study
words.example: He received his diploma at the graduation ceremony.

words.definitionEn: a long essay on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree
words.example: Her dissertation on climate change policy was highly praised by the committee.

words.definitionEn: a person who leaves school or college before completing a course
words.example: The school implemented programs to reduce the dropout rate among at-risk students.

words.definitionEn: a course or subject that students can choose to study, rather than being compulsory
words.example: Students may take elective courses in fields such as art or music.

words.definitionEn: the process of registering or being registered for a course or program
words.example: Enrollment for the fall semester opens in July.

words.definitionEn: activities that fall outside the regular academic curriculum
words.example: Participating in extracurricular activities can enhance a student's university application.

words.definitionEn: the teaching staff of a university or college, or a department within it
words.example: The faculty of arts and sciences offers a wide range of majors.

words.definitionEn: grade point average; a numerical measure of a student's academic performance
words.example: To maintain his scholarship, he needs to keep his GPA above 3.5.

words.definitionEn: the successful completion of a course of study, especially at a university
words.example: After graduation, she plans to work in the non-profit sector.

words.definitionEn: involving learning through discovery and problem-solving rather than direct instruction
words.example: The heuristic method encourages students to find solutions on their own.

words.definitionEn: considering the whole person or system, rather than just separate parts
words.example: A holistic education aims to develop the intellectual, emotional, and social aspects of a student.

words.definitionEn: involving communication and active participation between the teacher and students
words.example: Interactive learning platforms have become popular in modern classrooms.

words.definitionEn: involving two or more academic disciplines
words.example: The university offers an interdisciplinary program combining business and technology.

words.definitionEn: a period of work experience offered by an organization for a limited period, often to students
words.example: She completed an internship at a marketing firm to gain practical experience.

words.definitionEn: an educational talk given to a group of students, especially at a university
words.example: The professor's lecture on quantum mechanics was both informative and engaging.

words.definitionEn: the ability to read and write
words.example: Improving literacy rates among adults is a key goal of the education program.

words.definitionEn: the formal process of enrolling in a college or university
words.example: Matriculation into the university requires a high school diploma or equivalent.

words.definitionEn: an experienced and trusted advisor who guides a less experienced person
words.example: Each graduate student is assigned a mentor who provides academic guidance.

words.definitionEn: the ability to understand and work with numbers
words.example: Basic numeracy skills are essential for everyday life and many jobs.

words.definitionEn: the method and practice of teaching, especially as an academic subject
words.example: Modern pedagogy emphasizes student-centered learning over traditional lectures.

words.definitionEn: a person of the same age, status, or ability as another, especially in a school context
words.example: Peer assessment can help students develop critical thinking skills.

words.definitionEn: the practice of taking someone else's work or ideas and passing them off as one's own
words.example: Universities have strict policies against plagiarism, and offenders may face expulsion.

words.definitionEn: relating to studies undertaken after completing a first degree
words.example: Many students pursue postgraduate degrees to specialize in their field.

words.definitionEn: designed to improve or correct a student's skills in a particular area
words.example: The school offers remedial classes for students who struggle with mathematics.

words.definitionEn: extremely thorough, exhaustive, or accurate; demanding
words.example: The rigorous academic program prepares students for competitive careers.

words.definitionEn: a financial award given to a student to help pay for education
words.example: She was awarded a full scholarship to study abroad.

words.definitionEn: a small group discussion or class on a particular topic, often at a university
words.example: The seminar on educational technology was attended by 20 graduate students.

words.definitionEn: an outline of the subjects, topics, and readings for a course
words.example: The syllabus for the course includes weekly readings and assignments.

words.definitionEn: a long piece of research-based writing submitted for a higher degree, such as a master's or doctorate
words.example: He defended his thesis on the history of economic thought successfully.

words.definitionEn: an official record of a student's academic performance and courses taken
words.example: Applicants must submit their official transcripts along with the application form.

words.definitionEn: the fee charged for instruction, especially at a college or private school
words.example: Rising tuition costs have made higher education less accessible for many families.

words.definitionEn: a small group session led by a tutor, often used to supplement lectures
words.example: The weekly tutorial gives students the chance to ask questions and discuss ideas.

words.meaningVi: sinh viên đại học chưa tốt nghiệp
words.definitionEn: a student at a college or university who is working towards a first degree
words.example: Undergraduates are required to complete a certain number of credit hours per semester.

words.definitionEn: the student who has the highest academic rank in a graduating class and delivers the farewell speech
words.example: The valedictorian gave an inspiring speech at the graduation ceremony.

words.definitionEn: relating to education that prepares students for a specific trade or career
words.example: Vocational training programs provide practical skills for jobs like plumbing or carpentry.

words.definitionEn: a place where children go to be taught
words.example: My younger sister started primary school last September.

words.definitionEn: a period of time when someone is taught a subject
words.example: We had an English lesson with a new teacher today.

words.definitionEn: school work that pupils do at home
words.example: I finished my maths homework before dinner last night.

words.definitionEn: a room where lessons take place in a school
words.example: The classroom was quiet while the students took their test.

words.definitionEn: a person who is studying at a school or university
words.example: Every student must bring a pencil case to the exam.

words.definitionEn: a person whose job is to teach
words.example: Our history teacher gave us a lot of useful advice.

words.definitionEn: to study previous lessons again before an exam
words.example: I need to revise for my biology exam this weekend.

words.definitionEn: a formal test of knowledge or ability
words.example: She passed her driving exam on the first attempt.

words.definitionEn: an area of study taught in a school or college
words.example: Maths is my favourite subject because it is logical.

words.definitionEn: an institution where students study for degrees
words.example: My cousin is going to a university in Edinburgh next year.

words.definitionEn: a series of lessons on a particular subject
words.example: I signed up for a short course in photography.

words.definitionEn: to go regularly to a school, class or event
words.example: Students must attend every lecture to pass the module.

words.definitionEn: a place where books can be read or borrowed
words.example: We spent the afternoon studying quietly in the library.

words.definitionEn: a short piece of writing on a particular topic
words.example: He wrote a long essay about the history of Vietnam.

words.definitionEn: to gain knowledge or skill through study or experience
words.example: Children learn to read much faster when they enjoy books.

words.definitionEn: facts and skills that a person has gained through learning
words.example: Her broad knowledge of science impressed every member of the panel.

words.definitionEn: the person in charge of running a school
words.example: The headteacher spoke to parents about the new timetable.

words.definitionEn: a book that is used to teach a particular subject
words.example: Please open your textbook at page twelve before we begin the lesson.

words.definitionEn: a plan showing when lessons or events take place
words.example: The new timetable puts maths on Monday mornings.

words.definitionEn: to succeed in an exam or test
words.example: I was so nervous, but I finally passed the test.

words.meaningVi: học sinh (tiểu học, trung học cơ sở)
words.definitionEn: a child who is taught at a school
words.example: Each pupil in the class received a certificate for good attendance.

words.definitionEn: a teacher who gives individual lessons to a student
words.example: She hired a tutor to help her prepare for the IELTS speaking test.

words.definitionEn: to officially register as a student on a course
words.example: Over two hundred students enrolled in the new engineering course.

words.definitionEn: careful study carried out to discover new facts
words.example: Her research on learning habits was published in a journal.

words.definitionEn: to gain a diploma or certificate that allows you to work in a field
words.example: After three years of training, he qualified as a nurse.

words.definitionEn: to focus all your attention on one thing
words.example: It is hard to concentrate when the room is so noisy.

words.definitionEn: the reason why someone wants to do something
words.example: Strong motivation is often the key to mastering a language.

words.definitionEn: comments that tell someone how well they are doing
words.example: The teacher gave useful feedback on each student's draft.

words.definitionEn: involving real activity rather than only theory
words.example: The course includes practical sessions in the laboratory every week.

words.definitionEn: a teacher who gives lectures at a university
words.example: Our lecturer explained the theory with several real examples.

words.meaningVi: bài tập trong quá trình học
words.definitionEn: assignments completed during a course that count towards the final grade
words.example: Coursework accounts for forty percent of the final mark.

words.meaningVi: kỷ luật, lĩnh vực học thuật
words.definitionEn: controlled behaviour, or a branch of academic study
words.example: Good discipline in class helps students focus on their work.

words.definitionEn: to move or progress at the same speed or level as others
words.example: Some students struggled to keep up with the fast-paced lessons.

words.definitionEn: careful and hard-working in your studies or work
words.example: She was diligent about revising every evening before the test.

words.definitionEn: eager to know or learn about something
words.example: Curious children often ask questions that surprise their parents.

words.definitionEn: relating to mental processes such as thinking, learning and memory
words.example: Cognitive development in early childhood depends heavily on play and interaction.

words.definitionEn: a system in which people advance according to their ability
words.example: Critics argue that the examination system falls short of a true meritocracy.

words.definitionEn: to provide temporary support that helps learners reach a higher level
words.example: Teachers scaffold difficult tasks by breaking them into smaller steps.

words.meaningVi: điều chỉnh theo từng đối tượng
words.definitionEn: to adapt teaching so that it suits the needs of different learners
words.example: Good teachers differentiate their lessons to meet each student's needs.

words.meaningVi: học bổng sinh hoạt, trợ cấp
words.definitionEn: a fixed regular payment given to a student or trainee
words.example: The university awarded her a monthly stipend for her research.

words.definitionEn: a high level of skill or knowledge in a particular area
words.example: Applicants must demonstrate proficiency in English before enrolling.

words.meaningVi: năng khiếu, khả năng bẩm sinh
words.definitionEn: a natural ability to learn a particular skill
words.example: Her aptitude for mathematics became clear at a very young age.

words.definitionEn: based on observation or experiment rather than on theory
words.example: The study provides empirical evidence that group work improves retention.

words.definitionEn: to strengthen what has already been learned or achieved
words.example: Regular practice helps learners consolidate new vocabulary over time.

words.definitionEn: to provide evidence that supports a claim
words.example: Students must substantiate every argument with credible sources.

words.definitionEn: a group of students who start a course together
words.example: Our cohort was the largest the university had ever admitted.

words.definitionEn: something that is required before one can take a course or do something
words.example: Basic algebra is a prerequisite for the advanced physics module.

words.meaningVi: bậc đại học, sau trung học
words.definitionEn: relating to education that follows secondary school
words.example: Tertiary education has expanded rapidly across most developing countries.

words.meaningVi: khắc phục lỗ hổng kiến thức
words.definitionEn: to help learners correct gaps or weaknesses in their knowledge
words.example: The tutor remediated the weak students before the final examination.

words.definitionEn: careful and thorough in doing one's work or duties
words.example: She is a conscientious student who never misses a deadline.

words.definitionEn: a determined attempt to achieve something difficult
words.example: Her endeavour to learn Japanese earned her a scholarship.

words.definitionEn: relating to schools, universities or formal study
words.example: His scholastic achievements earned him admission to a top university.

words.definitionEn: a set of criteria used to assess student work
words.example: The teacher shared a detailed rubric before the writing assignment.

words.meaningVi: học bổng nghiên cứu sau đại học
words.definitionEn: a funded position that allows advanced study or research
words.example: He was awarded a research fellowship at the institute.

words.definitionEn: relating to the methods and practice of teaching
words.example: The workshop explored new pedagogical approaches to language teaching.

words.meaningVi: ăn nói rành mạch, lưu loát
words.definitionEn: able to express ideas clearly and fluently
words.example: The debate team was articulate and confident in every round.

words.meaningVi: sự tìm hiểu, nghiên cứu điều tra
words.definitionEn: a careful investigation carried out to discover facts
words.example: Inquiry-based learning encourages students to ask their own questions.

words.definitionEn: showing great attention to small details
words.example: The examiners were meticulous when they checked each answer sheet.

words.definitionEn: learning by repetition and memorisation without understanding
words.example: Rote learning can help memorise facts, but it rarely builds deep understanding.

words.meaningVi: trường cũ, mái trường đã đào tạo mình
words.definitionEn: the school, college or university that a person attended
words.example: She returned to her alma mater to give a lecture on linguistics.

words.definitionEn: a theory holding that learners build knowledge through experience and reflection
words.example: Constructivism argues that students learn best by actively exploring ideas.

words.definitionEn: relating to the subjects and courses in a school or college programme
words.example: Many universities offer extensive co-curricular activities alongside lectures.

words.definitionEn: to encourage interest, enthusiasm or activity
words.example: Engaging discussions can stimulate curiosity and critical thinking in classrooms.

words.meaningVi: gieo, nuôi dưỡng (thói quen, giá trị)
words.definitionEn: to gradually teach someone a belief, habit or value
words.example: Teachers should instil a love of reading in every young child.

words.definitionEn: dealing with problems in a practical, sensible way
words.example: The university took a pragmatic approach to reducing student dropout rates.

words.meaningVi: mang tính suy ngẫm, phản tư
words.definitionEn: thinking carefully about one's own experiences in order to learn
words.example: Reflective journals help students evaluate what they have learned each week.

words.definitionEn: to absorb new information and understand it fully
words.example: Students need time to assimilate complex ideas before they are tested.

words.meaningVi: học bổng hỗ trợ tài chính
words.definitionEn: a sum of money given to a student who needs financial help
words.example: She received a bursary that covered most of her living expenses.

words.meaningVi: thuộc trí tuệ, mang tính trí thức
words.definitionEn: relating to the mind and to reasoning or thinking
words.example: Debates offer intellectual challenges that sharpen students' reasoning skills.

words.meaningVi: minh hoạ, là ví dụ điển hình
words.definitionEn: to be a clear and typical example of something
words.example: Her thesis exemplifies the rigour expected of postgraduate researchers.

words.definitionEn: expressed clearly and easy to understand
words.example: Her lucid explanation made the complex theory easy to follow.

words.definitionEn: attended by all participants of a conference or meeting
words.example: The conference opened with a plenary session on digital learning.

words.definitionEn: having or showing great knowledge gained through study
words.example: The erudite professor could quote from dozens of ancient texts.

words.definitionEn: overly concerned with minor rules, details or correctness
words.example: The examiner was so pedantic about punctuation that candidates complained.

words.meaningVi: bí truyền, chỉ người trong nghề mới hiểu
words.definitionEn: understood by only a small number of people with special knowledge
words.example: The seminar focused on esoteric theories of medieval philosophy.

words.definitionEn: to make something unclear or harder to understand, often on purpose
words.example: Dense jargon can obfuscate the central argument of an essay.

words.definitionEn: having a clear understanding and sharp insight into situations
words.example: The perspicacious tutor noticed the misconception before the student did.

words.definitionEn: having keen judgement and sound practical wisdom
words.example: The sagacious headteacher advised the staff to listen before deciding.

words.meaningVi: người thầy giáo mang tính giáo điều
words.definitionEn: a teacher, often one who is strict and insists on rigid methods
words.example: The old pedagogue insisted that every student memorise the entire poem.

words.definitionEn: a person with expert knowledge across many different subjects
words.example: Leonardo was a polymath whose notebooks cover anatomy, engineering and art.

words.definitionEn: a person of great learning, especially in a specialist field
words.example: The savant gave a lecture that baffled even senior academics.

words.meaningVi: sự chú giải, diễn giải văn bản
words.definitionEn: a detailed critical explanation or interpretation of a text
words.example: Students spent weeks on the close exegesis of a single poem.

words.definitionEn: the theory and methodology of interpreting texts and meaning
words.example: Her thesis applies modern hermeneutics to classical legal documents.

words.meaningVi: người tài tử, làm nghiệp dư
words.definitionEn: a person who takes up a subject superficially rather than seriously
words.example: He was a dilettante who studied many subjects but mastered none.

words.definitionEn: remarkably great in size, amount or ability
words.example: The child showed a prodigious talent for mathematics at age six.

words.meaningVi: suy luận logic, lập luận có hệ thống

words.example: Careful ratiocination is required to solve the puzzle's final clue.

words.definitionEn: tending to wander from one topic to another rather than staying focused
words.example: Her discursive style made the essay difficult to follow.

words.definitionEn: clever but misleading arguments intended to deceive
words.example: The debater's reasoning was pure sophistry and collapsed under scrutiny.

words.definitionEn: making very high demands on a person's effort or skill
words.example: The doctoral programme is exacting, and many candidates withdraw early.

words.definitionEn: expressed so clearly that it is easy to understand
words.example: His pellucid prose made even the most abstract theory accessible.

words.meaningVi: sự kèm cặp, dưới sự hướng dẫn
words.definitionEn: instruction and guidance given to someone by a tutor or mentor
words.example: She flourished under the tutelage of a renowned composer.

words.definitionEn: a person who has taught themselves without formal instruction
words.example: As an autodidact, he mastered Latin by reading old manuscripts alone.

words.meaningVi: phát triển sớm, thông minh vượt tuổi
words.definitionEn: unusually advanced or mature for one's age
words.example: The precocious student started university at only fifteen.

words.meaningVi: uyên áo, ít người biết đến
words.definitionEn: little known and difficult to understand
words.example: The lecture drew on recondite sources that few scholars had read.

words.definitionEn: very hard to understand and of interest only to a few people
words.example: The abstruse mathematics in the appendix deterred most readers.

words.meaningVi: miệt mài nghiên cứu đến khuya
words.definitionEn: to study or work diligently, often late into the night
words.example: He would lucubrate by lamplight until the early hours of the morning.

words.definitionEn: covering a very wide range of knowledge in great detail
words.example: Her encyclopaedic memory astonished everyone in the seminar.

words.definitionEn: relating to knowledge and the ways in which it can be justified
words.example: The essay examines the epistemic status of expert testimony.

words.definitionEn: to think deeply and carefully about something for a long time
words.example: She ruminated on the professor's remarks long after the lecture ended.

words.meaningVi: thiên về trí óc, trừu tượng
words.definitionEn: appealing to the intellect rather than to the emotions
words.example: The novel is cerebral, demanding sustained concentration from its readers.

words.definitionEn: excessive concern with minor rules, details or formal correctness
words.example: Her pedantry about citation formats frustrated her co-authors.

words.meaningVi: sự sáng sủa, rõ ràng trong diễn đạt
words.definitionEn: clarity of expression that makes writing easy to understand
words.example: Perspicuity is the hallmark of good academic writing.

words.definitionEn: showing dedicated and persistent effort over a long period
words.example: The sedulous student rewrote every draft until it was flawless.

words.definitionEn: showing great care, attention and perseverance in one's work
words.example: Assiduous revision over several months secured her place at Oxford.

words.definitionEn: the ability to make quick and accurate judgements
words.example: Her business acumen helped the school win a major grant.

words.definitionEn: clear, logical and convincing in argument
words.example: The examiner praised the cogent structure of her argument.

words.definitionEn: to make something clear by explaining it in detail
words.example: The tutor elucidated the theory with a simple diagram.

words.meaningVi: trình bày chi tiết, giải thích
words.definitionEn: to explain a theory or idea in careful detail
words.example: He expounded his theory of learning over three long lectures.

words.meaningVi: tóm lược, nhắc lại các ý chính
words.definitionEn: to summarise and repeat the main points of something
words.example: Before the exam, the lecturer recapitulated the key concepts.

words.definitionEn: to teach someone to accept a set of beliefs without question
words.example: Critics warned that the textbook sought to indoctrinate young readers.

words.definitionEn: the quality of having keen judgement and practical wisdom
words.example: Her sagacity made her an invaluable adviser to the dean.

words.definitionEn: deep learning acquired through extensive study
words.example: His erudition was evident in every chapter of the monograph.

words.meaningVi: chủ nghĩa mập mờ, cố tình che giấu tri thức
words.definitionEn: the deliberate keeping of knowledge from people or making it obscure

words.definitionEn: insisting on one's beliefs as absolute truths and refusing to consider alternatives
words.example: The dogmatic lecturer refused to consider any alternative interpretation of history.

words.definitionEn: representing the perfect or most typical example of something
words.example: He was the quintessential scholar, lost in books from dawn till dusk.

words.meaningVi: không thể diễn tả bằng lời
words.definitionEn: too great or extreme to be expressed in words

words.meaningVi: phát biểu huênh hoang, lên lớp dài dòng
words.definitionEn: to express opinions at length in a pompous, self-important way
words.example: The professor loved to pontificate on subjects far outside his expertise.

words.meaningVi: dùng từ dài, văn phong cầu kỳ
words.definitionEn: characterised by the use of long, polysyllabic words
words.example: His sesquipedalian prose delighted specialists but baffled ordinary undergraduates.

words.meaningVi: lưu động, dạy ở nhiều nơi
words.definitionEn: moving from place to place, especially a teacher who works at several schools
words.example: The peripatetic music teacher travels between four schools every week.

words.definitionEn: slow and heavy, lacking lightness or ease in style
words.example: The ponderous prose of the dissertation made it a chore to finish.

name: Environment
blurb: Ô nhiễm, biến đổi khí hậu, bảo tồn

words.definitionEn: the presence of harmful substances in the environment
words.example: Industrial pollution has severely impacted the quality of local rivers.

words.definitionEn: the release of gases or substances into the atmosphere
words.example: The government has set strict limits on carbon emissions from factories.

words.definitionEn: a substance that makes something impure or polluted
words.example: Chemical contaminants in groundwater pose a serious health risk.

words.definitionEn: the removal of trees from a forested area
words.example: Deforestation in the Amazon accelerates climate change.

words.definitionEn: the variety of plant and animal life in a habitat
words.example: Protecting biodiversity is essential for a healthy ecosystem.

words.definitionEn: a community of living organisms and their environment
words.example: Deforestation disrupts the entire ecosystem of the region.

words.definitionEn: able to be maintained without harming the environment
words.example: Sustainable farming practices help preserve soil quality.

words.definitionEn: derived from sources that are naturally replenished
words.example: Many countries are investing in renewable energy sources.

words.definitionEn: the protection of natural resources and wildlife
words.example: Conservation efforts have helped restore the population of endangered species.

words.definitionEn: the process of becoming worse or less valuable
words.example: Soil degradation reduces agricultural productivity.

words.definitionEn: the total amount of greenhouse gases emitted by an activity
words.example: Reducing your carbon footprint can be achieved by using public transport.

words.definitionEn: a gas that traps heat in the atmosphere, contributing to global warming
words.example: Methane is a potent greenhouse gas released by livestock.

words.definitionEn: the gradual increase in Earth's average temperature
words.example: Global warming is causing polar ice caps to melt at an alarming rate.

words.definitionEn: long-term shifts in temperatures and weather patterns
words.example: Climate change is one of the most pressing issues of our time.

words.definitionEn: a layer in the stratosphere that protects Earth from UV radiation
words.example: The ozone layer is gradually recovering thanks to international agreements.

words.definitionEn: the reduction in the amount or quality of something
words.example: The depletion of natural resources threatens future generations.

words.definitionEn: a natural fuel such as coal or gas formed from ancient organisms
words.example: Burning fossil fuels releases large amounts of carbon dioxide.

words.definitionEn: to make less severe or serious
words.example: We need to mitigate the effects of industrial pollution on local communities.

words.definitionEn: to adjust to new conditions, especially environmental changes
words.example: Coastal cities must adapt to rising sea levels.

words.definitionEn: the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties or shocks
words.example: Building community resilience is crucial for coping with natural disasters.

words.definitionEn: caused or influenced by human activity
words.example: Anthropogenic emissions are the primary driver of global warming.

words.definitionEn: to make a problem or situation worse
words.example: Deforestation exacerbates the effects of climate change.

words.definitionEn: relating to the relationships between organisms and their environment
words.example: The oil spill caused an ecological disaster in the region.

words.definitionEn: a substance that pollutes the environment
words.example: Factories must filter pollutants before releasing wastewater.

words.definitionEn: water that flows over land and carries pollutants into water bodies
words.example: Agricultural runoff containing fertilizers causes algal blooms in lakes.

words.definitionEn: rainfall with high acidity due to pollutants like sulfur dioxide
words.example: Acid rain damages forests and acidifies lakes.

words.definitionEn: a mixture of smoke and fog, often caused by air pollution

words.definitionEn: having an unwanted reaction to a particular food, substance or thing

words.definitionEn: a vehicle designed to carry sick or injured people to hospital

words.definitionEn: action taken to stop a disease or problem from occurring

words.definitionEn: a medical test used to detect illness before symptoms appear

words.definitionEn: the process of returning to health after an illness or injury

words.definitionEn: feeling unsteady and as if everything is spinning around you

words.definitionEn: a life-threatening reaction of the body to a severe infection

words.definitionEn: a condition causing painful swelling and stiffness in the joints

words.definitionEn: a condition causing gradual loss of memory and thinking abilities

words.definitionEn: the branch of medicine dealing with the nervous system and its disorders

words.definitionEn: the branch of medicine that deals with the study and treatment of cancer

words.definitionEn: relating to the medical care of babies, children and young people

words.definitionEn: relating to the medical care of elderly people

words.definitionEn: the rate of illness or disease within a population

words.definitionEn: the number of deaths in a population over a given period

words.definitionEn: how often a particular disease occurs in a population

words.definitionEn: the proportion of a population that has a condition at a given time

words.definitionEn: a condition that makes a particular treatment unsafe for a patient

words.definitionEn: the regular use of several medicines by one patient at the same time

words.definitionEn: an abnormal area of tissue caused by injury or disease

words.definitionEn: an abnormal mass of tissue that may be benign or malignant

words.definitionEn: medication that causes loss of feeling or consciousness during surgery

words.definitionEn: a medicine that relieves pain without causing unconsciousness

words.definitionEn: effective against viruses, or used to treat a viral infection

words.definitionEn: a dangerous drop in body temperature caused by prolonged cold exposure

words.definitionEn: a heavy loss of blood from a damaged blood vessel

words.definitionEn: a medical action taken to improve a patient's condition

words.definitionEn: emergency treatment to restore breathing and heartbeat

words.definitionEn: the community of microorganisms living in a particular environment, such as the gut

words.definitionEn: the complete set of genetic material in an organism

words.definitionEn: a measurable substance that indicates a biological state or disease

words.definitionEn: the spread of a disease from one person or animal to another

words.definitionEn: the use of drugs to calm a patient or make them drowsy

words.definitionEn: showing no symptoms of a particular disease

words.meaningVi: phương pháp hỗ trợ điều trị

words.definitionEn: a restriction of blood supply to tissue, often to the heart or brain

words.definitionEn: conditions that follow and result from a previous disease or injury

words.definitionEn: the gradual period of recovery of health after an illness or operation

words.definitionEn: a state of tiredness, lack of energy or lack of interest

words.meaningVi: cảm giác khó chịu, mệt mỏi chung

words.definitionEn: loss of control over the coordination of muscle movements

words.definitionEn: difficulty in swallowing food or liquids

words.definitionEn: shortness of breath or difficulty in breathing

words.definitionEn: an abnormally slow heart rate, usually below sixty beats per minute

words.definitionEn: swelling caused by an excess of fluid trapped in body tissues

words.definitionEn: abnormal hardening or thickening of body tissue

words.definitionEn: the formation of excess fibrous tissue in an organ or tissue

words.definitionEn: chronic scarring of the liver that impairs its normal function

words.definitionEn: a serious infection of the intestines causing severe diarrhoea with blood

words.meaningVi: riêng biệt, mang tính đặc thù cá nhân

words.definitionEn: a sensation that you or your surroundings are spinning, causing loss of balance

words.definitionEn: a state of physical or mental weariness with little energy

words.meaningVi: giải toả, thanh lọc cảm xúc
words.definitionEn: providing emotional release that leaves a person feeling relieved

words.definitionEn: to relieve the symptoms of a disease without curing it

words.definitionEn: a medical term for an abnormally raised body temperature, or fever

words.definitionEn: extremely thin and weak, usually because of illness or hunger

words.definitionEn: a lack or loss of strength, often a sign of illness

words.meaningVi: khó tiêu, rối loạn tiêu hoá

words.meaningVi: sự bài niệu, tăng tiết nước tiểu

words.definitionEn: an abnormally low level of sugar in the blood

words.definitionEn: the systematic classification of diseases into groups

words.definitionEn: the study of the causes or origins of a disease
words.example: Researchers are still investigating the aetiology of this rare condition.

words.meaningVi: lành mạnh, tốt cho sức khoẻ
words.definitionEn: favourable to health, pleasant and healthy to live in

words.definitionEn: having or relating to a raised body temperature or fever

words.definitionEn: to protect someone against a disease by injecting a vaccine

words.definitionEn: making a person physically weak for a long time

words.meaningVi: bệnh hoạn, liên quan đến bệnh tật

words.definitionEn: optimistic and cheerful, even in difficult circumstances

words.definitionEn: inflammation of the inside of the nose, causing sneezing and congestion

words.definitionEn: death and decay of body tissue due to lack of blood supply

words.definitionEn: a condition in which the skin and eyes turn yellow due to liver problems

words.meaningVi: trạng thái tâm thần bất động

words.meaningVi: mất khả năng cảm nhận niềm vui

name: Work and Careers
blurb: Nghề nghiệp, nơi làm việc, kỹ năng

words.definitionEn: a job or profession, especially as a regular means of earning money
words.example: An individual’s occupation can significantly influence their social status and quality of life.

words.definitionEn: a paid occupation that requires advanced education or specialised training
words.example: The teaching profession requires both subject knowledge and strong interpersonal skills.

words.definitionEn: all the people who are available to work in a particular organisation, area, or country
words.example: An ageing workforce may create serious challenges for the national pension system.

words.meaningVi: việc làm; tình trạng có việc
words.definitionEn: the state of having paid work
words.example: Stable employment enables people to plan their finances and support their families.

words.meaningVi: bằng cấp hoặc chứng chỉ chuyên môn

words.definitionEn: the rate at which goods or services are produced compared with the resources used
words.example: Flexible working arrangements may increase employee productivity in some industries.

words.definitionEn: payment or other financial rewards received for work

words.definitionEn: the act of moving an employee to a higher position or rank

words.definitionEn: a person whose role is to oversee the work of others

words.definitionEn: a system in which people or roles are ranked according to authority or importance

words.meaningVi: tinh thần hoặc hoạt động khởi nghiệp

words.example: Entrepreneurship can provide employment opportunities in regions with limited industries.

words.definitionEn: from a location away from the usual workplace

words.definitionEn: the place where people carry out their jobs

words.definitionEn: the ability to change or adapt easily to different circumstances

words.definitionEn: the act of working jointly with others to achieve a shared objective

words.meaningVi: năng lực thực hiện công việc

words.definitionEn: the ability to adjust successfully to new conditions or demands

words.definitionEn: the ability to act independently and make decisions without being told what to do

words.definitionEn: the obligation to accept responsibility for decisions, actions, and results

words.meaningVi: thuộc về quan hệ giữa người với người

words.meaningVi: sinh lợi, có thu nhập cao

words.definitionEn: the job or series of jobs that someone does over a long period of their life, often with opportunities for advancement

words.definitionEn: a particular job or role within an organization

words.definitionEn: a person responsible for controlling or administering an organization or part of it

words.definitionEn: a person with whom one works in a professional setting

words.definitionEn: a task or piece of work allocated to someone as part of their job

words.definitionEn: specialized knowledge or skill in a particular field

words.definitionEn: the process of learning skills or knowledge needed for a particular job or activity

words.definitionEn: a non-wage advantage provided by an employer, such as health insurance or paid leave

words.definitionEn: a written document that describes the results of work or an investigation

words.definitionEn: a short period of time during which you stop working to rest

words.definitionEn: to give part of your work or authority to someone else

words.definitionEn: shared by or involving all members of a group

words.example: Analysts questioned the long-term viability of the small firm's business model.

words.definitionEn: to use something to maximum advantage in order to achieve a goal
words.example: The sales team learned to leverage social media to reach new customers.

words.definitionEn: careful and persistent effort in doing one's work
words.example: Her diligence in checking every invoice saved the company thousands.

words.definitionEn: the ability to work well across many different tasks or roles
words.example: Employers value the versatility of staff who can handle several roles.

words.definitionEn: taking action in advance to deal with problems before they arise
words.example: A proactive manager spots risks early and plans solutions before they escalate.

words.definitionEn: able to recover quickly from difficulties or setbacks
words.example: The resilient team recovered quickly after losing its biggest client.

words.definitionEn: a firm that provides expert advice to other organisations for a fee
words.example: She left the bank to join a management consultancy in London.

words.meaningVi: đào tạo hội nhập nhân viên mới
words.definitionEn: the process of introducing new employees to their role and the organisation
words.example: Effective onboarding helps new staff feel confident within their first month.

words.meaningVi: kỳ nghỉ phép dài hạn có lương
words.definitionEn: a long period of paid or unpaid leave taken for study or rest
words.example: After ten years, the professor took a sabbatical to write her book.

words.meaningVi: biệt phái, điều động tạm thời
words.definitionEn: a temporary move of an employee to work for another organisation
words.example: He accepted a six-month secondment to the government's trade department.

words.definitionEn: to make a process or task happen more quickly
words.example: The manager asked the team to expedite the approval of the contract.

words.meaningVi: tiêu chuẩn so sánh, mốc chuẩn
words.definitionEn: a standard or point of reference against which performance can be measured
words.example: The firm used industry averages as a benchmark for staff salaries.

words.definitionEn: a large company made up of several different businesses
words.example: The conglomerate employs thousands of workers across many industries.

words.definitionEn: a person who holds a lower rank and works under another person's authority
words.example: The manager praised his subordinates for their hard work during the audit.

words.definitionEn: a right or privilege that belongs to a particular person or position
words.example: Hiring the final candidate is the prerogative of the department head.

words.definitionEn: the quality of being trusted and believed by others
words.example: Her credibility grew after she delivered every project on time.

words.meaningVi: làm thêm việc khác ngoài giờ
words.definitionEn: to work a second job, often secretly, in addition to a main job
words.example: Many teachers moonlight as tutors to earn extra money during the evenings.

words.meaningVi: cắt giảm nhân sự, thu hẹp chi tiêu
words.definitionEn: the reduction of costs and staff in a company facing financial difficulty
words.example: Retrenchment in the printing division affected more than two hundred employees.

words.definitionEn: the act of ending someone's employment, often because of misconduct
words.example: The tribunal found that his dismissal was unfair and ordered compensation.

words.meaningVi: toà án lao động, hội đồng xét xử
words.definitionEn: a body appointed to hear and decide disputes, such as employment cases
words.example: The former employee took his case to the employment tribunal last spring.

words.meaningVi: có trách nhiệm ủy thác, tín thác
words.definitionEn: involving trust and a duty to act in another person's best interests
words.example: Directors have a fiduciary duty to act honestly with company funds.

words.definitionEn: a move to a lower position or rank within an organisation
words.example: He accepted a demotion rather than lose his job during the restructuring.

words.definitionEn: the act of choosing someone for a job or position
words.example: The board announced the appointment of a new chief financial officer.

words.definitionEn: the process of obtaining goods, services or equipment for an organisation
words.example: The procurement team negotiated lower prices with three different suppliers.

words.meaningVi: nhà thầu, người nhận hợp đồng
words.definitionEn: a person or company that agrees to do work for another under contract
words.example: The city hired a private contractor to repair the old bridge.

words.definitionEn: a well-paid job that requires little or no real work
words.example: Critics called the board seat a sinecure for a former minister.

words.meaningVi: chủ nghĩa thân quen, cất nhắc người nhà
words.definitionEn: favouring relatives or friends with jobs, regardless of their merit
words.example: Nepotism in hiring damaged morale among the more qualified applicants.

words.definitionEn: the practice of appointing close friends to positions of power
words.example: Cronyism in promotions led many talented staff to leave the company.

words.definitionEn: excessively eager to please superiors, in a servile way
words.example: The obsequious assistant agreed with every suggestion from the director.

words.definitionEn: flattering people in authority in order to gain personal advantage
words.example: His sycophantic emails to the chief executive embarrassed the whole team.

words.definitionEn: shy and lacking confidence in one's own abilities
words.example: The diffident junior analyst rarely spoke up during team meetings.

words.definitionEn: using very few words, often in a way that seems abrupt
words.example: The laconic manager replied to the long report with a single word.

words.meaningVi: cẩn trọng từng chi tiết, đúng quy tắc
words.definitionEn: showing great attention to formal rules and correct procedure
words.example: The punctilious accountant checked every receipt against the ledger twice.

words.definitionEn: persisting tirelessly and never giving up despite difficulties
words.example: The indefatigable sales director visited every branch in a single month.

words.definitionEn: hard-working and diligent in one's job or studies
words.example: The industrious staff completed the audit weeks before the deadline.

words.definitionEn: failing to produce the intended result or effect
words.example: The ineffectual committee met often but achieved very little.

words.definitionEn: motivated only by money rather than by loyalty or principle
words.example: Some staff criticised the mercenary attitude of recruits chasing bonuses.

words.meaningVi: thiên hướng nghề nghiệp, sứ mệnh
words.definitionEn: a strong feeling that a particular job or work is especially suited to you
words.example: For her, teaching was a true vocation rather than just a job.

words.meaningVi: công việc nhàm chán, nặng nhọc
words.definitionEn: hard, boring and monotonous work that feels exhausting
words.example: Endless data entry was pure drudgery that nobody on the team enjoyed.

words.definitionEn: involving a great deal of effort, responsibility or difficulty
words.example: The onerous reporting duties left the small team little time for projects.

words.definitionEn: long, slow and boring, often because it is repetitive
words.example: Reconciling the accounts by hand was a tedious task that took days.

words.definitionEn: lacking brightness, energy or excitement
words.example: The lacklustre performance review failed to inspire any real improvement.

words.definitionEn: excessive pride or self-confidence that often leads to failure
words.example: The chief executive's hubris blinded him to the warnings from his team.

words.meaningVi: đối thủ không thể đánh bại, số phận trừng phạt
words.definitionEn: a rival or cause of downfall that is hard to defeat
words.example: The upstart competitor became the company's nemesis in the local market.

words.meaningVi: điều bị ghét bỏ, điều cấm kỵ
words.definitionEn: something that is strongly detested or completely unacceptable
words.example: Layoffs by text message were anathema to the company's founding values.

words.meaningVi: bộ máy quan liêu, thủ tục rườm rà
words.definitionEn: complicated administrative procedures that slow down decisions and work
words.example: Excessive bureaucracy meant that a simple purchase took three weeks to approve.

words.meaningVi: khúm núm, cúi đầu nịnh bợ
words.definitionEn: to behave with exaggerated respect or obedience towards a superior
words.example: She refused to kowtow to the manager just to win his approval.

words.definitionEn: to behave in a servile way towards someone important in order to gain favour
words.example: Several staff toady to the director in the hope of a promotion.

words.definitionEn: to show exaggerated affection or flattery in order to win favour
words.example: The consultants fawn over the client's every comment in meetings.

words.definitionEn: cleverly manipulative and willing to deceive others to achieve power
words.example: The rival executive employed machiavellian tactics to win the top job.

words.meaningVi: mưu kế, kế hoạch khéo léo
words.definitionEn: a clever plan or trick used to gain an advantage over others
words.example: His stratagem to win the contract involved offering free training for the client.

words.definitionEn: having little or no money, especially over a long period
words.example: The impecunious graduate took two part-time jobs to pay the rent.

words.definitionEn: extremely poor, or unwilling to spend money
words.example: The penurious owner refused to pay for training, so staff learned on their own.

words.definitionEn: a salary, fee or other payment received from employment or office
words.example: The board approved an increase in the director's annual emoluments.

words.meaningVi: quyền lợi phụ, đãi ngộ thêm
words.definitionEn: an extra benefit or perk given to someone because of their job
words.example: A company car is a common perquisite for senior managers in many firms.

words.definitionEn: to protest strongly or argue against a decision or action
words.example: The union representative remonstrated with management about the unsafe conditions.

words.meaningVi: bằng lòng, chấp nhận miễn cưỡng
words.definitionEn: to accept or agree to something reluctantly, without objecting
words.example: The team acquiesced to the new schedule, though many disliked it.

words.definitionEn: apparently, as far as can be seen or claimed publicly
words.example: The meeting was ostensibly about budgets, but it was really about promotions.

words.definitionEn: to calm someone who is angry or upset, often by making concessions
words.example: The manager offered flexible hours to mollify the frustrated staff.

words.definitionEn: to use vague or ambiguous language in order to avoid committing to a view
words.example: When asked about redundancies, the director began to equivocate.

words.definitionEn: showing a lack of courage or determination when facing difficulties
words.example: The pusillanimous board postponed every hard decision until it was too late.

words.definitionEn: to try to gain someone's favour by flattering or pleasing them
words.example: He tried to ingratiate himself with the partners by praising every idea.

words.definitionEn: behaving as if one is better than others and showing disdain
words.example: The supercilious supervisor ignored the questions of junior staff.

words.definitionEn: extremely bad and obvious, in a way that is shocking
words.example: The egregious error in the payroll cost the firm a large sum.

words.definitionEn: unlucky, or unfortunate and having no success at all
words.example: The hapless intern was blamed for a mistake made by someone else.

words.definitionEn: to exclude someone from a group or social circle deliberately
words.example: Staff who reported the fraud were quietly ostracised by their colleagues.

words.definitionEn: showing little interest or enthusiasm in anything
words.example: Many apathetic employees simply waited for the working day to end.

words.definitionEn: moving or working slowly and without energy
words.example: Sales were sluggish all year, despite the new marketing campaign.

words.definitionEn: appearing calm and unconcerned, even when a situation is serious
words.example: The nonchalant manager shrugged off the warnings about the budget overrun.

words.definitionEn: dissatisfied and irritated, often about working conditions
words.example: Disgruntled workers gathered outside the office to protest the pay cut.

words.meaningVi: dỗ dành, tán tỉnh để thuyết phục
words.definitionEn: to persuade someone to do something by gentle flattery or coaxing
words.example: The director cajoled reluctant clients into signing the new contract.

words.definitionEn: bitter, cruel and full of hatred in tone or content
words.example: The vitriolic online comments about the decision upset the entire team.

name: Society
blurb: Cộng đồng, bất bình đẳng, chuẩn mực

words.definitionEn: the state of being unequal, especially in terms of rights, opportunities, or wealth.
words.example: The government must address the growing inequality in access to education.

words.meaningVi: chuẩn mực, quy tắc xã hội
words.definitionEn: a standard or pattern of behavior that is typical or expected within a group or society.
words.example: In many societies, it is a norm to greet others with a handshake.

words.definitionEn: a group of people living in the same place or having a particular characteristic in common.
words.example: The local community came together to support the victims of the flood.

words.definitionEn: the unjust treatment of different categories of people, especially on the grounds of race, age, or sex.
words.example: Laws against racial discrimination have been strengthened in many countries.

words.definitionEn: a preconceived opinion that is not based on reason or actual experience.
words.example: Prejudice against immigrants often stems from lack of understanding.

words.definitionEn: a widely held but fixed and oversimplified image or idea of a particular type of person or thing.
words.example: It is important to challenge negative stereotypes about minority groups.

words.definitionEn: the presence of, or support for the presence of, several distinct cultural or ethnic groups within a society.
words.example: Multiculturalism has enriched many societies but also sparked debates about national identity.

words.definitionEn: the state of being diverse; variety, especially in terms of culture, ethnicity, or background.
words.example: Workplace diversity can lead to greater creativity and innovation.

words.definitionEn: the practice of ensuring that people feel they belong and are valued in a group or society.
words.example: Social inclusion programs aim to reduce the marginalization of disadvantaged groups.

words.definitionEn: the process of preventing someone or something from being part of a group or society.
words.example: Long-term unemployment can lead to social exclusion.

words.meaningVi: sự gạt ra bên lề, thiệt thòi
words.definitionEn: the process of relegating a group or individual to a less important or powerless position within society.
words.example: The marginalization of indigenous communities has historical roots in colonialism.

words.definitionEn: the hierarchical arrangement of social classes or groups within a society.
words.example: Social stratification often determines an individual's life chances and opportunities.

words.meaningVi: giai cấp, tầng lớp xã hội
words.definitionEn: a system of ordering society based on status, wealth, or occupation.
words.example: The working class has historically fought for better labor rights.

words.meaningVi: hệ thống thứ bậc, phân cấp
words.definitionEn: a system in which members of a society are ranked according to their status or authority.
words.example: The social hierarchy in many traditional societies is rigid and difficult to change.

words.definitionEn: a special right, advantage, or immunity granted or available only to a particular person or group.
words.example: White privilege is a concept that refers to the unearned advantages enjoyed by white people in some societies.

words.definitionEn: prolonged cruel or unjust treatment or control of a group of people.
words.example: The struggle against oppression is a central theme in many social movements.

words.definitionEn: the action of treating someone unfairly in order to benefit from their work or resources.
words.example: Child labor is a form of exploitation that violates human rights.

words.definitionEn: unity or agreement of feeling or action, especially among individuals with a common interest.
words.example: The protesters showed solidarity by marching together for social justice.

words.definitionEn: the action or fact of forming a united whole, especially in a social context.
words.example: Social cohesion is essential for a peaceful and prosperous society.

words.definitionEn: the process of bringing together people from different groups into a unified society.
words.example: Successful integration of immigrants requires language training and job opportunities.

words.definitionEn: the process by which a minority group adopts the customs and attitudes of the dominant culture.
words.example: Assimilation policies have often been criticized for erasing cultural diversity.

words.definitionEn: the action of setting someone apart from others, especially based on race or religion.
words.example: Racial segregation in schools was declared unconstitutional in many countries.

words.meaningVi: khu ổ chuột, khu biệt lập
words.definitionEn: a part of a city, especially a slum area, occupied by a minority group that is isolated from the rest of society.
words.example: Living in a ghetto can limit access to quality education and healthcare.

words.meaningVi: tầng lớp dưới đáy xã hội
words.definitionEn: a social class consisting of people who are in the lowest position in the social hierarchy and often face poverty and unemployment.
words.example: The underclass is often trapped in a cycle of poverty and deprivation.

words.definitionEn: a system in which people are chosen and rewarded based on their ability and effort rather than their wealth or social class.
words.example: Education is often seen as a key to achieving meritocracy.

words.meaningVi: chủ nghĩa bình quân, bình đẳng
words.definitionEn: the belief that all people are equal and should have equal rights and opportunities.
words.example: Egalitarianism is a core principle of many democratic societies.

words.definitionEn: the advocacy of women's rights on the grounds of equality of the sexes.
words.example: Feminism has helped to achieve significant progress in gender equality, but challenges remain.

words.definitionEn: a system of society or government in which men hold the power and women are largely excluded from it.
words.example: The patriarchy has historically limited women's roles in the public sphere.

words.definitionEn: the state in which access to rights or opportunities is unaffected by gender.
words.example: Promoting gender equality is essential for sustainable development.

words.definitionEn: the concept of equal treatment and opportunity for people of all races.
words.example: The movement for racial equality has gained momentum in recent years.

words.definitionEn: the concept of fair and just relations between individuals and society, including the distribution of wealth and opportunities.
words.example: Social justice requires addressing systemic inequalities in education and healthcare.

words.meaningVi: phúc lợi, an sinh xã hội
words.definitionEn: the health, happiness, and prosperity of a person or group, or government programs that provide financial support to people in need.
words.example: The welfare state in many European countries provides a safety net for the unemployed.

words.definitionEn: the state of being extremely poor, lacking the means to meet basic needs.
words.example: Poverty is often linked to lack of access to education and healthcare.

words.definitionEn: the state of having a great deal of money, wealth, or material possessions.
words.example: The affluence of the upper class contrasts sharply with the poverty of the underclass.

words.definitionEn: the condition of not having a permanent place to live, often due to poverty or lack of affordable housing.
words.example: Homelessness is a visible sign of social inequality in many cities.

words.definitionEn: an action or omission that constitutes an offense and is punishable by law.
words.example: High crime rates are often associated with areas of high unemployment.

words.meaningVi: sự lệch chuẩn, hành vi lệch lạc
words.definitionEn: behavior that violates social norms or expectations.
words.example: Sociologists study deviance to understand how societies define and enforce norms.

words.meaningVi: sự tuân thủ, phù hợp với chuẩn mực
words.definitionEn: the act of matching attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors to group norms or societal expectations.
words.example: Conformity can be both a source of social stability and a barrier to change.

words.definitionEn: the action or fact of obeying a law, rule, or request, or conforming to a standard.
words.example: Compliance with social norms is often rewarded by acceptance within the group.

words.definitionEn: the power or right to give orders, make decisions, and enforce obedience.
words.example: Societies rely on legitimate authority to maintain order and stability.

words.definitionEn: the process of enabling individuals or groups to gain control over their own lives and decisions.
words.example: Women's empowerment is a key goal of many development programs.

words.definitionEn: a select group of people who have more power, wealth, or influence than the rest of society.
words.example: The political elite often have access to better education and healthcare.

words.meaningVi: quần chúng, đông đảo người dân
words.definitionEn: the ordinary people in society, as opposed to the elite or privileged class.
words.example: The mass media can influence the opinions of the masses on social issues.

words.meaningVi: dư luận, ý kiến công chúng
words.definitionEn: the views of the general population on a particular issue, often measured by polls.
words.example: Public opinion plays a crucial role in shaping government policies.

words.definitionEn: a collective effort by a group of people to bring about social or political change.
words.example: The civil rights movement was a major social movement that fought for racial equality.

words.meaningVi: hoạt động xã hội, chủ nghĩa hành động
words.definitionEn: the use of direct action or vigorous campaigning to bring about social or political change.
words.example: Activism can take many forms, from petitions to protests.

words.definitionEn: the practice of offering time and services to help others without financial reward.
words.example: Volunteerism strengthens community bonds and provides vital services.

words.definitionEn: the desire to promote the welfare of others, expressed especially by the generous donation of money to good causes.
words.example: Philanthropy plays a significant role in funding social programs and research.

words.definitionEn: the responsibilities of a citizen, such as voting, obeying laws, and contributing to the community.
words.example: Voting is considered a fundamental civic duty in a democracy.

words.definitionEn: an implicit agreement among members of a society to cooperate for social benefits, often involving giving up some freedoms in exchange for security.
words.example: The social contract theory underpins modern ideas of government and citizenship.

words.definitionEn: a person who legally belongs to a particular country
words.example: Every citizen has the right to vote in national elections.

words.definitionEn: all the people who live in a particular area
words.example: The population of the city has grown rapidly over the past decade.

words.definitionEn: a person who lives near or next to you
words.example: Our neighbour always helps us when we need something.

words.definitionEn: all the people within a society who are of about the same age
words.example: Young people from this generation often prefer messages to phone calls.

words.definitionEn: relating to the countryside rather than to towns or cities
words.example: Many rural families still depend on farming for their income.

words.definitionEn: relating to towns and cities rather than the countryside
words.example: Urban areas often face serious traffic jams during the rush hour.

words.definitionEn: a small group of houses and other buildings in the countryside
words.example: The village has only one shop and a small primary school.

words.definitionEn: a large group of people gathered together in one place
words.example: A large crowd gathered outside the stadium before the match.

words.definitionEn: an official instruction saying what people must or must not do
words.example: Every member of the club must follow the rules carefully.

words.definitionEn: a feeling of admiring someone and treating them with care
words.example: Children should show respect to their elders at family gatherings.

words.definitionEn: the way a person acts, especially in public or with other people
words.example: Her polite behaviour impressed everyone at the community meeting.

words.meaningVi: phép lịch sự, cách cư xử
words.definitionEn: polite ways of behaving towards other people in social situations
words.example: Good manners are important when you meet new people for the first time.

words.definitionEn: a relationship between people who like and trust each other
words.example: Their friendship grew stronger after years of working together.

words.definitionEn: the legal union between a husband and a wife
words.example: Many couples delay marriage until they have stable jobs and savings.

words.meaningVi: tổ chức từ thiện; lòng từ thiện
words.definitionEn: an organisation that collects money and helps people in need
words.example: She works for a charity that supports homeless children in the city.

words.definitionEn: treating people equally and without favouritism or prejudice
words.example: It is only fair that everyone shares the household chores equally.

words.definitionEn: having the same rights, status or value as other people
words.example: All students should have equal access to good education.

words.definitionEn: willingness to accept opinions and behaviour that differ from your own
words.example: Schools should teach tolerance towards people with different beliefs.

words.definitionEn: informal talk about other people's private lives, often unkind
words.example: The office was full of gossip about the new manager.

words.definitionEn: a line of people waiting one behind another for something
words.example: We waited in a long queue for the bus to arrive.

words.definitionEn: a person you have never met or do not know
words.example: Parents should teach children not to talk to strangers.

words.definitionEn: something a person is morally or legally required to do
words.example: Citizens have a duty to pay their taxes on time.

words.definitionEn: a freedom that people are legally or morally entitled to have
words.example: Everyone has the right to express their opinions freely.

words.definitionEn: the way a person or group chooses to live
words.example: A healthy lifestyle includes regular exercise and balanced meals.

words.definitionEn: a person who is invited to visit someone's home or attend an event
words.example: The hosts welcomed each guest with a warm smile at the door.

words.meaningVi: sự xa lánh, cảm giác bị cô lập
words.definitionEn: a feeling of being isolated from society or from other people
words.example: Young migrants often experience alienation in unfamiliar cities.

words.definitionEn: the state of being separated from other people or places
words.example: Elderly people living alone can suffer from social isolation.

words.definitionEn: strong social disapproval attached to a particular condition or behaviour
words.example: Many people still face stigma when they admit to mental illness.

words.definitionEn: strong dislike or fear of people from other countries
words.example: Xenophobia can lead to violence against foreign workers.

words.definitionEn: the fact of belonging to a particular ethnic group
words.example: The survey asked respondents to state their age and ethnicity.

words.definitionEn: the qualities that make a person or group distinct from others
words.example: Her strong sense of identity came from her local community.

words.definitionEn: a duty to do something because of a law, promise or moral reason
words.example: Employers have an obligation to protect the health of their staff.

words.definitionEn: a strong negative reaction by many people against a change or decision
words.example: The new policy sparked a fierce public backlash across the country.

words.meaningVi: từ cơ sở, từ dưới lên
words.definitionEn: coming from ordinary people rather than from leaders or organisations
words.example: The protest was a grassroots movement led by local volunteers.

words.definitionEn: relating to the structure and characteristics of a population
words.example: The country faces a serious demographic change as its population ages.

words.meaningVi: phân biệt đối xử theo tuổi
words.definitionEn: prejudice or discrimination against people because of their age
words.example: Ageism makes it hard for older workers to find new jobs.

words.meaningVi: sự thượng lưu hoá khu dân cư
words.definitionEn: the process by which poorer areas become wealthier and displace older residents
words.example: Gentrification has pushed many families out of the old district.

words.definitionEn: the growth of towns and cities as more people move there from rural areas
words.example: Rapid urbanization has increased pressure on housing and transport.

words.definitionEn: the state of relying on someone or something for support or money
words.example: Some families face financial dependency on government benefits.

words.definitionEn: a lack of the things people need for a decent standard of living
words.example: Children from areas of deprivation often have fewer opportunities.

words.definitionEn: a state of being successful, healthy and having plenty of money
words.example: The town enjoyed real prosperity after the new factory opened.

words.definitionEn: a particular area of a town or city where people live
words.example: The whole neighbourhood holds a street party every summer.

words.definitionEn: unselfish concern for the welfare and needs of other people
words.example: Her altruism inspired many volunteers to join the local charity.

words.definitionEn: the unhappy feeling of being alone or without companionship
words.example: Loneliness is a growing problem among older citizens in many countries.

words.definitionEn: a strong desire to achieve something important in life
words.example: Many young people share the aspiration of owning their own home.

words.definitionEn: the ability to move between social classes, jobs or places
words.example: Education can improve social mobility for children from poor families.

words.definitionEn: dominance of one group over others, especially in culture or politics
words.example: The dominant class maintains its hegemony through education and the media.

words.definitionEn: a layer or level of society made up of people with similar status
words.example: Each stratum of society had distinct habits and social expectations.

words.definitionEn: the state of being deprived of rights, influence or political voice
words.example: Economic disenfranchisement often drives people away from voting.

words.definitionEn: the act of excluding a person from a group or community
words.example: Her ostracism from the village shocked her family deeply.

words.definitionEn: involvement with others in an action that is considered wrong
words.example: Silence can amount to complicity in an unjust social system.

words.definitionEn: a lack of interest, enthusiasm or concern about important matters
words.example: Voter apathy has grown steadily in many long-established democracies.

words.meaningVi: bên lề, ở rìa xã hội
words.definitionEn: relating to people or groups positioned at the edge of mainstream society
words.example: Marginal groups often lack access to basic public services.

words.definitionEn: firmly established over a long time and difficult to change
words.example: Entrenched prejudice against women takes generations to overcome completely.

words.definitionEn: the coexistence of different groups with different beliefs in one society
words.example: Healthy democracy depends on pluralism and open public debate.

words.definitionEn: treating adults like children by making decisions on their behalf
words.example: State paternalism can limit the freedom of individual citizens.

words.definitionEn: favouring relatives or friends when giving jobs or positions of power
words.example: Nepotism undermined public trust in the appointment process.

words.definitionEn: polite and respectful behaviour in social and public interaction
words.example: Public debate has lost much of its civility in recent years.

words.definitionEn: concerned only with a narrow local area or group, ignoring wider issues
words.example: Parochial attitudes made it difficult for the town to accept newcomers.

words.definitionEn: isolated from outside influences and narrow in outlook

words.definitionEn: not secure or stable, especially in relation to work or income

words.definitionEn: shared by or belonging to all members of a community

words.definitionEn: to organise people or resources for a particular purpose

words.definitionEn: the general mood, beliefs and spirit characteristic of a particular period

words.meaningVi: tình trạng vô chuẩn xã hội

words.definitionEn: showing off wealth or status in a way intended to impress others

words.definitionEn: obvious and shocking, in a way that is completely unacceptable

words.definitionEn: developing gradually in a harmful way that is hard to notice

words.definitionEn: the middle class, especially owners of property, capital and businesses

words.meaningVi: hay gây chia rẽ bè phái

words.meaningVi: kẻ thô thiển, thờ ơ với văn hoá

words.definitionEn: understood or implied without being stated openly

words.definitionEn: excessive pride or self-confidence that often leads to a fall

words.definitionEn: the customs and conventions regarded as fundamental by a social group

words.meaningVi: không khí thân mật, vui vẻ

words.definitionEn: the ability to endure pain or hardship without showing strong emotion

words.meaningVi: chức vụ ăn lương không việc

words.definitionEn: a general dislike or distrust of other people and of humanity

words.definitionEn: public disgrace or harsh criticism for shameful behaviour

words.definitionEn: a person who is rejected or avoided by other members of society

words.definitionEn: a person who takes the law into their own hands to punish wrongdoers

words.definitionEn: exemption from punishment, harm or consequences for one's actions

words.definitionEn: the quality of doing good, showing kindness and generosity to others

words.definitionEn: a feeling of weariness and dissatisfaction caused by lack of interest

words.definitionEn: motivated by a desire to help others rather than by self-interest

words.definitionEn: deliberate betrayal of someone's trust or loyalty

words.meaningVi: bè phái, khép kín trong nhóm
