words.example: The demographic changes after the famine altered the size of the workforce.

words.definitionEn: The mass departure of many people from a place, usually because of difficulty.
words.example: The exodus from the drought-stricken valley left few families in the village.

words.meaningVi: cộng đồng người sống xa quê hương
words.definitionEn: A community of people who have spread away from their original homeland.

words.example: Hysteresis losses in the transformer core waste part of the energy as heat.

words.definitionEn: The opposition that a circuit offers to alternating current, caused by inductance or capacitance.
words.example: High reactance in the cable reduces the power that reaches the distant substation.

words.definitionEn: The total opposition to alternating current in a circuit, combining resistance and reactance.
words.example: Matching the impedance of the inverter to the grid minimises energy losses.

words.definitionEn: The ability of a component to store electric charge, measured in farads.
words.example: Higher capacitance allows the circuit to store more charge for smoother output.

words.definitionEn: The property of a circuit that opposes changes in the current flowing through it.
words.example: The coil's inductance smooths out sudden spikes in the electric current.

words.definitionEn: A device that converts alternating current into direct current.
words.example: A rectifier at the charging station turns grid power into direct current for batteries.

words.definitionEn: A device that converts direct current into alternating current for household supply.
words.example: The solar inverter feeds the power from the roof into the household supply.

words.definitionEn: A device that changes the voltage of alternating current by electromagnetic induction.
words.example: The transformer steps up the voltage so that power travels efficiently across the country.

words.definitionEn: A heavy rotating wheel that stores kinetic energy and smooths out variations in motion.
words.example: The engineers installed a flywheel to store energy for brief power interruptions.

words.definitionEn: A capacitor that stores much more energy than ordinary capacitors and charges very quickly.
words.example: A supercapacitor can deliver a burst of power to start the motor in seconds.

words.definitionEn: A liquid or gel that conducts electricity through the movement of ions, used in batteries.
words.example: The electrolyte in the battery must stay stable across a wide range of temperatures.

words.definitionEn: An electrode where reduction occurs, typically the positive terminal of a battery during discharge.
words.example: Lithium ions move from the anode to the cathode when the battery discharges.

words.definitionEn: An electrode where oxidation occurs, typically the negative terminal of a battery during discharge.
words.example: Graphite is widely used as the anode in modern lithium-ion batteries.

words.definitionEn: A substance that speeds up a chemical reaction without being used up in the process.
words.example: A platinum catalyst helps convert hydrogen and oxygen into water in fuel cells.

words.definitionEn: Relating to entropy, the measure of disorder or unavailable energy in a system.
words.example: Every entropic process leaves less useful energy than before for future work.

words.definitionEn: The branch of physics dealing with heat, work, and the energy relationships in physical systems.
words.example: Thermodynamics explains why no engine can convert all its heat into useful work.

words.definitionEn: A measure of the total heat content of a system at constant pressure.
words.example: The enthalpy of combustion for natural gas determines how much heat it releases.

words.definitionEn: The maximum useful work that can be extracted from a system as it reaches equilibrium with its surroundings.
words.example: Analysing exergy shows where the plant loses the most useful energy.

words.definitionEn: Relating to heat energy, especially the amount of heat a fuel produces when burned.
words.example: The calorific value of wood varies with its moisture content and species.

words.meaningVi: phép tính hoá học theo tỉ lượng
words.definitionEn: The calculation of the quantities of reactants and products in a chemical reaction.
words.example: Stoichiometry tells engineers how much oxygen a fuel needs for complete combustion.

words.definitionEn: A form of the same chemical element with a different number of neutrons in its nucleus.
words.example: Uranium isotope enrichment is central to the operation of many nuclear reactors.

words.definitionEn: The spontaneous emission of radiation from the unstable nuclei of certain atoms.
words.example: Radioactivity decreases over time as unstable atoms gradually decay into stable forms.

words.definitionEn: The time taken for half of the radioactive atoms in a sample to decay.
words.example: The half-life of this isotope is about thirty years, so it stays hazardous for long.

words.definitionEn: Capable of undergoing nuclear fission when struck by neutrons.
words.example: Uranium-235 is fissile, so it sustains the chain reaction inside the reactor core.

words.meaningVi: phản ứng tổng hợp hạt nhân
words.definitionEn: The joining of light atomic nuclei to form a heavier nucleus, releasing huge amounts of energy.
words.example: Nuclear fusion powers the sun, combining hydrogen nuclei into helium.

words.definitionEn: Relating to a material that obeys Ohm's law, with current directly proportional to voltage.
words.example: Ohmic resistors keep the relationship between voltage and current linear.

words.definitionEn: The standard unit of energy, equal to the work done by one newton moving one metre.
words.example: One kilowatt-hour equals 3.6 million joules, a useful figure for energy bills.

words.example: Gleaning was once a customary right that allowed the poor to gather grain.

words.definitionEn: A symbiotic association between fungal threads and the roots of a plant.
words.example: Mycorrhiza helps crops absorb phosphorus more efficiently from poor soils.

words.definitionEn: Excess nutrients in water that cause algae to bloom and deplete oxygen.
words.example: Fertiliser runoff has caused severe eutrophication in the lake that supplies drinking water.

words.definitionEn: A small landowner who farms his own land, historically in England.
words.example: The yeoman tilled his modest farm and sold surplus grain at the local market.

words.definitionEn: The rural region lying behind a coastal area, port or major city.
words.example: Fresh produce from the hinterland is trucked daily to the city's wholesale markets.

words.meaningVi: độ tơi xốp của đất canh tác
words.definitionEn: The condition of cultivated soil, especially its texture and suitability for planting.
words.example: Good tilth allows roots to penetrate easily and water to infiltrate the soil.

words.definitionEn: An abundant supply of good things, especially food and produce.
words.example: The autumn market offered a cornucopia of pumpkins, grapes, apples and fresh cheese.

words.meaningVi: sự phong phú, mùa bội thu
words.definitionEn: A generous supply of something good, especially natural produce or harvest.
words.example: The generous bounty of the summer harvest kept the village well fed through winter.

words.definitionEn: Relating to the countryside, or to the raising of livestock on grassland.
words.example: Pastoral communities move their herds across the plateau according to the seasons.

words.meaningVi: đồng quê thanh bình lý tưởng
words.definitionEn: Idyllically rural and simple, in an idealised, peaceful way.
words.example: The painter depicted an arcadian landscape of shepherds and golden wheat fields.

words.definitionEn: Relating to woods or forests, or characterised by trees.
words.example: We walked along a sylvan path shaded by oaks and beech trees.

words.definitionEn: To bear fruit, or to make something productive and fruitful.
words.example: The orchard fructified early this year after an unusually mild spring.

words.definitionEn: To begin to grow and develop from a seed or spore.
words.example: Most seeds germinate best when the soil is warm and consistently moist.

words.definitionEn: A farmer who works land owned by another and pays rent with a share of the crop.
words.example: The sharecropper gave half of every harvest to the landowner as rent.

words.definitionEn: A very large agricultural estate, typically worked by dependent labourers.
words.example: The latifundium dominated the valley, employing hundreds of tenants and seasonal workers.

words.definitionEn: The legal right to use and enjoy the produce of another's property.
words.example: The tenant held the usufruct of the orchard for the duration of the lease.

words.definitionEn: The planting of trees on land that has not recently been forested.
words.example: Afforestation projects on the barren hills have gradually stabilised the eroded slopes.

words.definitionEn: The replanting of trees in areas where forests were previously cleared.
words.example: Reforestation of the watershed has improved water quality and reduced flooding downstream.

words.definitionEn: To live in or move to the countryside, away from urban life.
words.example: Retired professionals often rusticate in quiet villages to grow vegetables and keep bees.

words.definitionEn: The seasonal movement of livestock between lowland and highland pastures.
words.example: Transhumance routes across the Alps were once travelled by herders every summer.

words.meaningVi: canh tác sinh học động lực
words.definitionEn: Describing farming that treats the farm as a self-sustaining living system.
words.example: The biodynamic vineyard uses compost preparations and follows a lunar planting calendar.

words.definitionEn: A resting state in which seeds or plants pause growth until conditions improve.
words.example: Seed dormancy protects the embryo until the rains arrive and the soil softens.

words.definitionEn: The gradual deterioration of a plant or leaf as it ages.
words.example: Leaf senescence in autumn releases nutrients that the tree stores in its roots.

words.meaningVi: thời kỳ sinh học theo mùa
words.definitionEn: The study of seasonal natural events such as flowering, leafing and migration.
words.example: Phenology records show that spring blossoms now appear several days earlier than before.

words.definitionEn: A shoot or bud cut from one plant and grafted onto the rootstock of another.
words.example: The nurseryman grafted a scion of the heritage apple onto a sturdy rootstock.

words.definitionEn: The root system of a plant onto which another variety is grafted.
words.example: Dwarf rootstock produces smaller trees that are easier to harvest by hand.

words.definitionEn: Producing abundant offspring, crops or new growth; highly fertile.
words.example: The fecund volcanic soil supports dense forests and bountiful vegetable gardens.

words.definitionEn: Describing soil that crumbles easily and is easy to work with tools.
words.example: A friable loam is ideal for root vegetables such as carrots and beetroot.

words.definitionEn: Fertile soil containing a balanced mixture of sand, silt and clay.
words.example: The gardener enriched the poor clay with compost to create a crumbly loam.

words.definitionEn: A soft, lime-rich clay or earth often used to improve acidic farmland.
words.example: Farmers spread marl over the acidic fields to raise the soil's alkalinity.

words.definitionEn: An old term for a farmer who cultivates and works the land.
words.example: The husbandman rose before dawn to tend his sheep and mend the fences.

words.definitionEn: Shaping hillsides into level steps to grow crops and reduce soil erosion.
words.example: Centuries of terracing have transformed the mountain slopes into productive rice fields.

words.definitionEn: A plant adapted to survive in very dry environments with little water.
words.example: Cacti and succulents are xerophytes that store water in thick stems and leaves.

words.definitionEn: A plant that tolerates high salt levels in soil or water.
words.example: Some halophytes can be cultivated on coastal land affected by seawater intrusion.

name: Animals and Wildlife
blurb: Loài, môi trường sống, tuyệt chủng

words.definitionEn: the natural environment in which an animal or plant lives
words.example: The destruction of natural habitats is a major threat to biodiversity.

words.definitionEn: a group of living organisms that can reproduce with each other
words.example: Many species are at risk of extinction due to human activities.

words.definitionEn: an animal that hunts and kills other animals for food
words.example: The introduction of predators can disrupt the local ecosystem.

words.definitionEn: an animal that is hunted and killed by another animal
words.example: The prey population declines when predator numbers increase.

words.definitionEn: the seasonal movement of animals from one region to another
words.example: Bird migration is a remarkable natural phenomenon.

words.definitionEn: the state of no longer existing as a species
words.example: Human activity has accelerated the rate of extinction.

words.definitionEn: illegal hunting of wild animals
words.example: Poaching remains a serious problem for endangered species.

words.definitionEn: the process of changing to suit new conditions
words.example: Animals develop adaptations to survive in harsh environments.

words.definitionEn: the variety of plant and animal life in a particular habitat
words.example: Tropical rainforests support high levels of biodiversity.

words.definitionEn: the protection of natural resources and wildlife
words.example: Conservation efforts have helped save several species from extinction.

words.definitionEn: a community of interacting organisms and their physical environment
words.example: A healthy ecosystem provides essential services for human beings.

words.definitionEn: at risk of becoming extinct
words.example: The giant panda is no longer considered endangered.

words.definitionEn: the clearing of forests for other uses
words.example: Deforestation destroys the habitat of countless animals.

words.definitionEn: a person who hunts illegally
words.example: Poachers kill rhinos for their horns.

words.definitionEn: a place where wildlife is protected
words.example: The sanctuary provides a safe haven for injured animals.

words.definitionEn: likely to become endangered in the near future
words.example: The IUCN lists this species as threatened.

words.meaningVi: nhân giống trong điều kiện nuôi nhốt
words.definitionEn: breeding of animals in controlled environments to help preserve species
words.example: Captive breeding programs have been successful for the California condor.

words.meaningVi: khu dự trữ động vật hoang dã
words.definitionEn: an area set aside for the protection of wild animals
words.example: The wildlife reserve covers thousands of hectares.

words.definitionEn: non-native species that cause harm to the ecosystem
words.example: Invasive species often outcompete native wildlife.

words.definitionEn: a person who works to protect the environment
words.example: Conservationists advocate for stricter wildlife protection laws.

words.definitionEn: a state of equilibrium in an ecosystem
words.example: Human activities can disrupt the ecological balance.

words.meaningVi: dễ bị tổn thương, dễ tuyệt chủng
words.definitionEn: at risk of becoming endangered
words.example: The species is classified as vulnerable on the IUCN Red List.

words.definitionEn: caused or influenced by humans
words.example: Anthropogenic factors are the main cause of biodiversity loss.

words.definitionEn: the local extinction of a species in a specific area
words.example: The extirpation of wolves from the region disrupted the food chain.

words.meaningVi: hành lang động vật hoang dã
words.definitionEn: a strip of habitat connecting isolated populations
words.example: Wildlife corridors help animals move between fragmented habitats.

words.definitionEn: a cold-blooded vertebrate animal that can live both in water and on land, such as frogs and salamanders.
words.example: Amphibians are highly sensitive to environmental changes, making them excellent bioindicators.

words.definitionEn: living or growing in water.
words.example: Aquatic ecosystems, such as coral reefs, support a vast array of marine life.

words.definitionEn: living in trees.
words.example: Arboreal animals, like monkeys and sloths, have strong limbs for climbing.

words.definitionEn: relating to birds.
words.example: Avian species exhibit a wide range of migratory behaviours.

words.definitionEn: to produce offspring.
words.example: Many birds breed in the spring to take advantage of abundant food resources.

words.definitionEn: a hole or tunnel dug by an animal for shelter.
words.example: Rabbits dig extensive burrow systems to protect themselves from predators.

words.definitionEn: the natural coloring or form that allows an animal to blend in with its surroundings.
words.example: The chameleon's ability to change its skin colour provides excellent camouflage.

words.definitionEn: an animal that feeds on other animals.
words.example: Lions are apex carnivores that play a crucial role in controlling prey populations.

words.definitionEn: active during the day.
words.example: Diurnal animals, such as most songbirds, rely on daylight for foraging.

words.definitionEn: the animals of a particular region, habitat, or geological period.
words.example: The fauna of the Amazon rainforest is incredibly diverse.

words.definitionEn: a young bird that has just developed feathers and is learning to fly.
words.example: Fledglings often leave the nest before they are fully capable of flight.

words.definitionEn: a group of birds or sheep.
words.example: A flock of geese flew south for the winter.

words.definitionEn: a newly hatched animal, especially a reptile or bird.
words.example: Sea turtle hatchlings instinctively crawl towards the ocean after emerging from their nests.

words.definitionEn: an animal that feeds on plants.
words.example: Herbivores such as deer and rabbits have digestive systems adapted to break down cellulose.

words.meaningVi: bầy đàn (động vật có vú lớn)
words.definitionEn: a group of animals, especially large mammals, that live together.
words.example: A herd of elephants can travel long distances in search of water.

words.definitionEn: to spend the winter in a dormant state.
words.example: Some bears hibernate for several months, relying on stored body fat.

words.definitionEn: a warm-blooded vertebrate animal that has hair or fur and feeds its young with milk.
words.example: Mammals are characterized by their ability to regulate body temperature internally.

words.definitionEn: to shed feathers, hair, or skin to make way for new growth.
words.example: Birds molt their feathers annually to maintain flight efficiency.

words.definitionEn: active during the night.
words.example: Many nocturnal animals, like owls and bats, have evolved enhanced senses of hearing and vision.

words.definitionEn: the young of an animal.
words.example: Parental care is crucial for the survival of offspring in many mammalian species.

words.definitionEn: an animal that eats both plants and animals.
words.example: Bears are omnivores, consuming berries, fish, and small mammals.

words.definitionEn: a group of wild animals, especially wolves, that hunt together.
words.example: Wolves hunt in packs to take down prey larger than themselves.

words.definitionEn: a cold-blooded vertebrate animal of a class that includes snakes, lizards, crocodiles, turtles, etc.
words.example: Reptiles are ectothermic and often bask in the sun to regulate their body temperature.

words.definitionEn: a large group of fish swimming together.
words.example: The shoal of herring moved swiftly to avoid the dolphins.

words.definitionEn: living on land.
words.example: Terrestrial animals have evolved various adaptations to cope with arid environments.

words.definitionEn: A living creature, such as a dog, horse or lion, that is not a human or plant.
words.example: Many children enjoy visiting the zoo to see unusual animals up close.

words.definitionEn: A warm-blooded animal with feathers and wings that usually can fly.
words.example: A small bird built its nest in the branches above our kitchen window.

words.definitionEn: A cold-blooded animal that lives in water and breathes through gills.
words.example: Hundreds of colourful fish swim around the coral reef every morning.

words.definitionEn: A small animal with six legs, a body in three parts, often with wings.
words.example: Bees and butterflies are insects that play an important role in pollination.

words.definitionEn: A wild animal related to dogs that hunts in groups in forests.
words.example: A lone wolf was spotted crossing the snowy valley at dawn.

words.definitionEn: A large, heavy wild animal with thick fur that eats fish, plants and honey.
words.example: A brown bear wandered close to the campsite searching for food overnight.

words.definitionEn: A small furry animal with long ears that lives in holes in the ground.
words.example: The rabbit darted into its hole when it heard the dog barking nearby.

words.definitionEn: A long, legless reptile that moves along the ground by sliding.
words.example: The hikers were warned to watch carefully for snakes in the tall grass.

words.definitionEn: A small jumping animal with smooth skin that lives near water.
words.example: After the spring rain, frogs filled the pond with loud, cheerful croaking.

words.definitionEn: A structure built by birds or insects to hold their eggs or young.
words.example: The sparrows built a nest from twigs, grass and feathers under the roof.

words.definitionEn: One of the light, soft growths that cover the body of a bird.
words.example: She found a bright blue feather lying on the path near the lake.

words.definitionEn: A sharp curved nail on the foot of an animal, used for grip or hunting.
words.example: The cat extended its sharp claws when it climbed the tall tree.

words.definitionEn: To chase and kill wild animals for food or sport.
words.example: Lions usually hunt at night when the temperature drops and prey is active.

words.definitionEn: To move through water by moving the arms, legs, or body.
words.example: Dolphins swim in groups and communicate with each other through clicking sounds.

words.definitionEn: A park where wild animals are kept for display and study.
words.example: The zoo recently welcomed two baby pandas from a research centre in China.

words.definitionEn: Animals and plants living freely in their natural environment.
words.example: Wildlife photographers often wait for hours to capture a rare moment.

words.definitionEn: The thick, soft hair that covers the body of many mammals.
words.example: The arctic fox changes the colour of its thick fur with the seasons.

words.definitionEn: The hard protective covering on the foot of a horse, deer or similar animal.
words.example: The deer's sharp hoof left a deep print in the muddy riverbank.

words.definitionEn: A long, pointed tooth that projects outside the mouth of some animals.
words.example: Elephant tusks have been illegally traded for centuries by ivory dealers.

words.definitionEn: A branched bony horn that grows on the head of a deer.
words.example: Each autumn, the male deer sheds its antlers and grows new ones.

words.definitionEn: One of the small hard plates that cover the skin of fish and reptiles.
words.example: The fish's silver scales shimmered as it swam beneath the surface.

words.definitionEn: An area of land that an animal defends and regards as its own.
words.example: The male lion marks its territory with scent to warn rivals away.

words.definitionEn: A hidden shelter or lair where a wild animal rests or raises its young.
words.example: The fox kept her cubs safe inside a den dug under the hedge.

words.definitionEn: The complete set of feathers covering a bird's body.
words.example: The male peacock displays its brilliant plumage to attract potential mates.

words.definitionEn: A large group of animals of the same kind living together in one place.
words.example: A colony of penguins huddled together against the freezing Antarctic wind.

words.definitionEn: To wander freely over a wide area without a fixed route.
words.example: Herds of bison once roamed the prairies in their millions across North America.

words.definitionEn: To search widely for food, especially plants or small animals.
words.example: Squirrels forage for nuts and seeds throughout the autumn months.

words.meaningVi: ăn xác thối, nhặt đồ ăn thừa
words.definitionEn: To search for and eat food that others have left or that is already dead.
words.example: Crows often scavenge rubbish bins for scraps of leftover food in the city.

words.definitionEn: To follow an animal slowly and quietly in order to catch it.
words.example: The tiger began to stalk the herd, keeping low behind the tall grass.

words.definitionEn: To feed on growing grass or herbs in a field or pasture.
words.example: Sheep graze on the hillside, keeping the grass short throughout summer.

words.definitionEn: To attract an animal or person by offering something tempting.
words.example: Anglers use bright lures to tempt trout into biting the hook.

words.definitionEn: To lie in warmth, especially sunlight, to raise body temperature.
words.example: Lizards bask on warm rocks in the morning before they begin hunting insects.

words.definitionEn: The act of hunting and killing other animals for food.
words.example: Heavy predation by foxes has reduced the local rabbit population sharply.

words.definitionEn: To come together with another animal to produce young.
words.example: Frogs gather at the pond in spring to mate and lay their eggs.

words.definitionEn: To move from one region to another, often seasonally, to find food or warmth.
words.example: Swallows migrate thousands of kilometres every autumn to reach warmer climates.

words.definitionEn: To enter a dormant state during hot or dry periods to conserve energy.
words.example: Some desert snails estivate during the hottest months to avoid drying out.

words.definitionEn: To release eggs into water, as fish and frogs do.
words.example: Salmon return to the rivers where they were born to spawn each autumn.

words.definitionEn: The specific role an organism plays within its ecosystem.
words.example: Each bird species occupies a distinct ecological niche in the forest canopy.

words.definitionEn: A close, long-term interaction between two different organisms that benefits both.
words.example: The relationship between cleaner fish and larger reef species is a classic symbiosis.

words.definitionEn: An organism that lives on or inside another organism and harms it.
words.example: Ticks are external parasites that feed on the blood of deer and dogs.

words.definitionEn: Moving regularly from place to place rather than settling permanently.
words.example: Many nomadic herders follow seasonal grazing routes across the steppe.

words.definitionEn: Tending to live in groups and enjoy the company of others.
words.example: Gregarious animals such as zebras rely on the herd for protection from predators.

words.definitionEn: Living or preferring to be alone rather than in a group.
words.example: The solitary tiger patrols a vast territory that overlaps with several other animals.

words.definitionEn: Able to inject a poison through bites or stings.
words.example: The venomous snake strikes quickly, so hikers should avoid disturbing it.

words.definitionEn: Naturally occurring in a particular region rather than introduced by humans.
words.example: The indigenous frogs of the island are threatened by newly introduced predators.

words.definitionEn: A species whose presence strongly affects the structure of its whole ecosystem.
words.example: Sea otters act as a keystone species by controlling sea urchin populations along the coast.

words.definitionEn: An animal that feeds on dead or decaying matter left by others.
words.example: Vultures are efficient scavengers that clean carcasses from the African plains.

words.definitionEn: The decaying flesh of dead animals, eaten by some birds and insects.
words.example: Vultures can detect carrion from great distances using their keen sense of smell.

words.meaningVi: sự bắt chước màu sắc để tự vệ
words.definitionEn: The resemblance of one species to another that helps it avoid being eaten.
words.example: Harmless hoverflies use mimicry to resemble stinging wasps and deter predators.

words.meaningVi: cảnh báo độc bằng màu sắc
words.definitionEn: Having bright colours that warn predators that the animal is poisonous.
words.example: The bright red colouring of the frog is aposematic, warning predators of its toxic skin.

words.definitionEn: A dramatic transformation in form during the life cycle of an animal.
words.example: The caterpillar undergoes metamorphosis inside the chrysalis before emerging as a butterfly.

words.definitionEn: The young, wingless form of an insect that hatches from an egg.
words.example: The larva feeds voraciously on leaves until it is ready to pupate.

words.definitionEn: A resting stage between larva and adult in many insects, often inside a case.
words.example: Inside the silk cocoon, the pupa slowly transforms into an adult moth.

words.definitionEn: A sweet liquid produced by flowers to attract pollinating insects and birds.
words.example: Hummingbirds hover over blossoms to drink nectar with their long, slender bills.

words.definitionEn: Staying in one place or moving very little during a particular period.
words.example: Unlike its migratory cousins, this sparrow is largely sedentary throughout the year.

words.definitionEn: The period during which a mother carries developing young before birth.
words.example: Elephant gestation lasts nearly two years, the longest of any land mammal.

words.definitionEn: A group of young born to an animal at the same time from one mother.
words.example: The mother wolf nursed her litter of five pups in a sheltered den.

words.definitionEn: The hard protective case in which a caterpillar changes into a butterfly.
words.example: A monarch chrysalis hangs from a leaf, glistening with a metallic green shell.

words.definitionEn: A silky protective casing spun by many insect larvae before they change form.
words.example: The moth spins a silken cocoon around itself before its transformation begins.

words.meaningVi: trạng thái lờ đờ, ngủ đông ngắn
words.definitionEn: A state of reduced activity and metabolism, used to conserve energy.
words.example: Hummingbirds can enter torpor overnight to conserve energy during cold nights.

words.definitionEn: A group of young birds or animals hatched and raised together.
words.example: The hen guarded her brood of chicks closely in the tall grass.

words.definitionEn: A hoofed mammal, such as a deer, horse or cow.
words.example: Antelopes and zebras are ungulates that graze across the African savanna.

words.definitionEn: A mammal that carries and nurses its young in a pouch on the belly.
words.example: Kangaroos are marsupials that give birth to tiny, underdeveloped young.

words.definitionEn: An eight-legged invertebrate such as a spider, scorpion or tick.
words.example: Scorpions are arachnids with pincers and a venomous sting in the tail.

words.definitionEn: An aquatic invertebrate with a hard shell, such as a crab, lobster or shrimp.
words.example: Freshwater crustaceans provide food for many species of fish and birds.

words.definitionEn: A marine mollusc with tentacles, such as an octopus or a squid.
words.example: The cephalopod can change its skin colour within seconds to blend into rocks.

words.definitionEn: Active mainly during twilight at dusk or dawn.
words.example: Rabbits are crepuscular, feeding most actively in the early morning and evening.

words.definitionEn: A hoofed animal that chews cud, such as a cow, goat or deer.
words.example: Cattle and goats are ruminants that digest tough grasses in several stomach chambers.

words.definitionEn: A large, thick-skinned mammal, such as an elephant or rhinoceros.
words.example: The pachyderm wallowed in the mud to cool down under the blazing afternoon sun.

words.definitionEn: The highest-ranking predator in a food chain, with few or no natural enemies.
words.example: The leopard is an apex predator, controlling populations of deer and wild pigs.

words.definitionEn: An animal that walks on four legs, such as a dog or horse.
words.example: Most mammals are quadrupeds, though humans and apes often walk upright.

words.meaningVi: lưỡng cư, sống hai môi trường
words.definitionEn: Able to live both on land and in water.
words.example: The amphibious crocodile hunts in rivers and rests on sun-warmed banks.

words.definitionEn: Feeding mainly on fish, as many herons, kingfishers and ospreys do.
words.example: The osprey is piscivorous, diving feet-first to snatch fish from the water.

words.meaningVi: tính trung thành với nơi sinh
words.definitionEn: The tendency of animals to return to the place where they were born.
words.example: Philopatry draws salmon back to the very stream where they hatched years earlier.

words.definitionEn: Describing fish that live in the sea but breed in fresh water.
words.example: Anadromous fish such as salmon ascend rivers to spawn after years at sea.

words.definitionEn: Describing fish that live in fresh water but breed in the sea.
words.example: Eels are catadromous, living in rivers before travelling to the ocean to breed.

words.definitionEn: The existence of two distinct forms or appearances within one species.
words.example: Sexual dimorphism makes male lions far larger and more maned than females.

words.definitionEn: A mating system in which one male mates with several females.
words.example: Polygyny is common among elephant seals, where dominant males control harems.

words.definitionEn: Born helpless and requiring extensive parental care, as many songbirds are.
words.example: Altricial chicks depend on their parents for food and warmth for several weeks.

words.meaningVi: tự lập sớm khi mới nở
words.definitionEn: Born relatively mature and mobile, able to feed themselves soon after hatching.
words.example: Precocial ducklings can swim and forage within hours of leaving the egg.

words.definitionEn: An animal whose body temperature depends mainly on external heat sources.
words.example: As an ectotherm, the lizard must bask in sunlight to warm its muscles.

words.definitionEn: An animal that generates its own body heat through metabolic processes.
words.example: Unlike reptiles, most birds and mammals are endotherms that regulate heat internally.

words.definitionEn: Hidden or concealed, especially as a form of camouflage.
words.example: The moth's cryptic wings resemble dead leaves, making it nearly invisible on bark.

words.definitionEn: Capable of flight; able to fly.
words.example: Volant mammals such as bats navigate in darkness using echolocation calls.

words.definitionEn: Adapted for leaping or jumping, as in grasshoppers and kangaroos.
words.example: Saltatorial locusts launch themselves across the field with powerful hind legs.

words.meaningVi: thích đào bới, sống dưới đất
words.definitionEn: Adapted for digging and living underground, like moles or badgers.
words.example: Fossorial rodents excavate elaborate tunnel systems beneath the grassland.

words.definitionEn: Adapted for running fast over open ground, as with cheetahs and horses.
words.example: Cursorial animals such as gazelles escape predators by sprinting across plains.

words.definitionEn: Adapted for swimming, typically through webbed feet or paddle-like limbs.
words.example: Penguins display natatorial adaptations, with flipper-shaped wings that propel them underwater.

words.definitionEn: Adapted for climbing trees or rock faces with specialised claws or grip.
words.example: Scansorial lizards cling effortlessly to vertical bark with their toe pads.

words.definitionEn: An animal that lives permanently in caves and has adapted to darkness.
words.example: Blind cave beetles are troglobites that have lost their eyes over many generations.

words.definitionEn: An animal whose diet consists mainly of worms.
words.example: Many shorebirds are vermivores, probing wet mud for worms with long beaks.

words.definitionEn: An animal that eats mainly fruit, playing a key role in seed dispersal.
words.example: Many tropical bats are frugivores that scatter seeds across the rainforest.

words.definitionEn: An animal that feeds mainly on seeds and grain.
words.example: Finches are granivores whose conical beaks are perfect for cracking seeds.

words.definitionEn: Feeding on blood, as in mosquitoes, leeches and vampire bats.
words.example: Hematophagous mosquitoes transmit malaria while feeding on the blood of humans.

words.definitionEn: The practice of eating insects as a regular part of the diet.
words.example: Entomophagy is common across Southeast Asia, where crickets and grubs are sold in markets.

words.meaningVi: côn trùng ký sinh gây chết vật chủ
words.definitionEn: An insect whose larvae develop inside or on a host and eventually kill it.
words.example: The wasp is a parasitoid whose larvae consume the caterpillar from inside.

words.definitionEn: Describing a relationship in which one partner benefits and the other is unaffected.
words.example: Barnacles living on whales form a commensal relationship that costs the host nothing.

words.definitionEn: A relationship in which two species both gain benefits from each other.
words.example: Mutualism between figs and wasps depends on each partner for reproduction.

words.definitionEn: Describing populations separated geographically, so they cannot interbreed.
words.example: Allopatric populations of the same lizard evolved different colours on separate islands.

words.definitionEn: Describing populations that live in the same area and may interbreed.
words.example: Sympatric finches diverged in beak shape after competing for the same seeds.

words.definitionEn: The capacity of an organism to produce a large number of offspring.
words.example: High fecundity allows fish to replace losses from fishing and predation quickly.

words.definitionEn: A disease transmitted naturally from animals to humans.
words.example: Scientists track zoonosis carefully, since many new human diseases originate in wildlife.

words.definitionEn: The ability of an organism to move freely from one place to another.
words.example: Low vagility means the frog rarely crosses the road to reach the next pond.

words.definitionEn: The evolutionary history and relationships among a group of organisms.
words.example: Genetic sequencing has clarified the phylogeny of the big cats over millions of years.

words.definitionEn: A group of organisms classified together at any level of taxonomy.
words.example: Biologists redefined the taxon after DNA evidence revealed hidden lineages.

words.definitionEn: Found naturally in only one particular region and nowhere else.
words.example: Madagascar hosts many endemic lemurs that exist nowhere else on Earth.

words.meaningVi: tập trung biểu diễn tán tỉnh
words.definitionEn: A courtship display in which males gather in one place to attract females.
words.example: Lekking grouse perform elaborate dances on the same patch of ground each spring.

words.definitionEn: The production of sound by rubbing body parts together, as crickets do.
words.example: Stridulation by male crickets attracts females during warm summer evenings.

words.definitionEn: Locating objects by emitting sounds and interpreting the returning echoes.
words.example: Dolphins use echolocation to find fish in murky water where vision is limited.

words.definitionEn: Describing a body part that has lost most of its original function.
words.example: The tiny vestigial wings of the flightless beetle are hidden beneath its hard shell.

words.definitionEn: Relating to turtles and tortoises, a group of reptiles with protective shells.
words.example: Chelonian eggs must incubate in warm sand for several months before hatching.

words.definitionEn: Having irregular patches of two colours, usually black and white.
words.example: The piebald horse stood out in the meadow with its irregular black and white patches.

words.definitionEn: The study of sounds produced by animals and how they communicate.
words.example: Bioacoustics researchers record whale songs to map migration patterns across oceans.

words.definitionEn: Living in the open ocean, away from the seabed or coastal waters.
words.example: Tuna and marlin are pelagic fish that roam vast distances across the open sea.

words.definitionEn: Living on or near the bottom of a sea, lake or river.
words.example: Benthic worms burrow into sediment, mixing nutrients into the riverbed below.

words.definitionEn: Tiny organisms drifting in water, forming the base of aquatic food webs.
words.example: Whales feed on plankton, straining huge quantities of water through baleen plates.

words.definitionEn: The wide, tidal mouth of a river where it meets the sea.
words.example: Migratory birds gather in the estuary to feed on crabs and worms.

words.definitionEn: Carrying developing eggs or young inside the body before birth.
words.example: The gravid female lizard searched for a warm, sheltered nest site.

words.meaningVi: noãn thai (trứng nở trong cơ thể)
words.definitionEn: Producing eggs that hatch inside the mother, so the young are born alive.
words.example: Many sharks are ovoviviparous, giving birth to fully formed young from eggs hatched internally.

words.definitionEn: Laying eggs that develop and hatch outside the mother's body.
words.example: Most birds and reptiles are oviparous, depositing eggs in nests or sand.

name: Weather and Climate
blurb: Mùa, thiên tai, nhiệt độ

words.definitionEn: A seasonal prevailing wind that brings heavy rainfall, especially in South Asia.
words.example: The monsoon season is crucial for agriculture in India, as it provides the majority of annual rainfall.

words.definitionEn: Relating to a region with moderate temperatures, not extremely hot or cold.
words.example: Temperate climates are often considered ideal for human habitation due to their mild weather patterns.

words.definitionEn: Relating to the region near the equator, characterized by warm temperatures year-round.
words.example: Tropical regions are known for their high humidity and abundant biodiversity.

words.definitionEn: Relating to the extremely cold region near the North Pole.
words.example: Arctic sea ice is melting at an alarming rate due to global warming.

words.definitionEn: A prolonged period of abnormally low rainfall, leading to a shortage of water.
words.example: Severe drought has devastated crop yields in the region, causing food shortages.

words.definitionEn: An overflow of water onto land that is usually dry, often caused by heavy rain or storm surges.
words.example: The catastrophic flood displaced thousands of residents and damaged infrastructure.

words.definitionEn: The amount of water vapor present in the air.
words.example: High humidity can make hot weather feel even more oppressive and uncomfortable.

words.definitionEn: Any form of water, such as rain, snow, or hail, that falls from the atmosphere to the Earth's surface.
words.example: The annual precipitation in this desert region is less than 100 millimeters.

words.definitionEn: A large, powerful storm with strong winds and heavy rain, forming over warm ocean waters.
words.example: The hurricane caused widespread destruction along the coast, with wind speeds exceeding 200 km/h.

words.definitionEn: A violent, rotating column of air that extends from a thunderstorm to the ground.
words.example: Tornadoes are capable of leveling entire neighborhoods in just a few minutes.

words.definitionEn: A severe snowstorm with strong winds, low visibility, and intense cold.
words.example: The blizzard forced the closure of all major highways and airports in the region.

words.definitionEn: A rapid flow of snow down a slope, often triggered by natural factors or human activity.
words.example: The avalanche buried several ski huts under tons of snow, requiring a massive rescue operation.

words.definitionEn: A prolonged period of excessively hot weather, often with high humidity.
words.example: The heatwave broke temperature records across Europe, leading to health warnings.

words.definitionEn: A sudden, short period of very cold weather.
words.example: The cold snap caused pipes to burst in many homes due to freezing temperatures.

words.definitionEn: A storm with hail, which are balls or lumps of ice that fall from the sky.
words.example: The hailstorm damaged cars and crops, with some hailstones as large as golf balls.

words.definitionEn: A mass of mud and other debris sliding down a slope, often after heavy rain.
words.example: Heavy rainfall triggered a mudslide that destroyed several houses in the hillside village.

words.definitionEn: A large, destructive fire that spreads quickly over vegetation, often in dry conditions.
words.example: The wildfire consumed thousands of acres of forest, releasing vast amounts of carbon dioxide.

words.meaningVi: bão nhiệt đới (Ấn Độ Dương, Thái Bình Dương)
words.definitionEn: A large-scale storm system with rotating winds, often forming in tropical regions.
words.example: The cyclone made landfall with destructive winds and torrential rain, causing widespread flooding.

words.definitionEn: The time when day and night are of equal length, occurring twice a year.
words.example: The spring equinox marks the beginning of longer days and warmer temperatures.

words.definitionEn: The time when the sun reaches its highest or lowest point, resulting in the longest or shortest day.
words.example: The summer solstice brings the longest daylight hours of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

words.definitionEn: The long-term increase in Earth's average temperature due to human activities, especially greenhouse gas emissions.
words.example: Global warming is causing glaciers to retreat and sea levels to rise at an unprecedented rate.

words.definitionEn: The trapping of heat in the atmosphere by gases such as carbon dioxide, causing the planet to warm.
words.example: The enhanced greenhouse effect, driven by human activities, is a primary cause of climate change.

words.definitionEn: The total amount of greenhouse gases emitted by an individual, organization, or product.
words.example: Reducing your carbon footprint by using public transport can help mitigate climate change.

words.definitionEn: A serious condition caused by overheating of the body, often due to prolonged exposure to high temperatures.
words.example: Heatstroke can be fatal if not treated promptly, especially during extreme heatwaves.

words.definitionEn: A dangerous condition where the body temperature drops below normal, often due to cold exposure.
words.example: Hypothermia is a major risk for hikers caught in sudden cold snaps without proper gear.

words.definitionEn: The long-term average weather conditions of a region, including temperature, precipitation, and wind patterns.
words.example: The climate of the Mediterranean region is mild and rainy in winter, which attracts many tourists.

words.definitionEn: The layer of gases surrounding the Earth, which influences weather and climate.
words.example: The atmosphere plays a crucial role in regulating the Earth's temperature by trapping heat.

words.definitionEn: Relating to the scientific study of weather and atmospheric conditions.
words.example: Meteorological data collected over decades helps scientists predict long-term climate trends.

words.definitionEn: A prediction of future weather conditions based on scientific analysis.
words.example: The weather forecast indicated a high probability of thunderstorms this afternoon.

words.definitionEn: An observable event or fact, especially in the natural world, such as a weather event.
words.example: El Niño is a climatic phenomenon that disrupts normal weather patterns worldwide.

words.definitionEn: The tendency of weather or climate to change or vary over time.
words.example: The variability of rainfall in this region makes agriculture particularly challenging.

words.definitionEn: A deviation from the normal or expected pattern, often used in climatology to describe unusual weather events.
words.example: The temperature anomaly recorded last month was 3°C above the historical average.

words.definitionEn: The process by which water vapor in the air turns into liquid water, forming clouds or fog.
words.example: Condensation occurs when warm, moist air comes into contact with a cold surface.

words.definitionEn: The process by which liquid water changes into water vapor, driven by heat from the sun.
words.example: High evaporation rates in arid regions contribute to the formation of salt flats.

words.definitionEn: A storm with thunder and lightning, typically accompanied by heavy rain or hail.
words.example: The sudden thunderstorm caused widespread power outages across the city.

words.definitionEn: A bright flash of light produced by electrical discharge in the atmosphere during a storm.
words.example: Lightning strikes can ignite wildfires, especially in dry forests.

words.definitionEn: A thick cloud of tiny water droplets suspended in the air near the ground, reducing visibility.
words.example: Dense fog delayed flights at the airport for several hours this morning.

words.definitionEn: A thin layer of ice crystals formed on surfaces when the temperature drops below freezing.
words.example: The early frost damaged many crops, causing significant losses for farmers.

words.definitionEn: Precipitation consisting of partly frozen rain, often hitting the ground as small ice pellets.
words.example: Sleet made the roads extremely slippery and dangerous for drivers.

words.definitionEn: Small balls of ice that fall from thunderstorms, often causing damage to property and crops.
words.example: Hail the size of golf balls pummeled the neighborhood, breaking windows and denting cars.

words.definitionEn: A very strong wind, typically between 34 and 40 knots on the Beaufort scale.
words.example: The gale uprooted several trees and overturned small boats in the harbor.

words.definitionEn: A scientist who studies weather and atmospheric conditions to make forecasts and understand climate.
words.example: The meteorologist warned that the incoming storm could bring record-breaking rainfall.

words.definitionEn: An instrument that measures atmospheric pressure, used to predict weather changes.
words.example: A rapidly falling barometer often signals an approaching storm or cyclone.

words.definitionEn: A line on a weather map connecting points of equal temperature.
words.example: The isotherm chart clearly showed a cold front moving southward across the continent.

words.definitionEn: Occurring or varying with the seasons of the year.
words.example: Seasonal variations in temperature and daylight affect plant growth cycles.

words.meaningVi: hàng ngày (về biến động nhiệt độ)
words.definitionEn: Relating to or occurring during the day, or describing daily cycles, often used for temperature range.
words.example: The diurnal temperature range in desert regions can exceed 20°C between day and night.

words.definitionEn: A small, localized area with different weather conditions from the surrounding region.
words.example: The garden's microclimate, sheltered by walls, allows tropical plants to thrive despite the cold winters.

words.definitionEn: Very severe or unusual, often used to describe weather events that are dangerous or record-breaking.
words.example: Extreme weather events, such as intense heatwaves and heavy rainfall, have become more frequent.

words.definitionEn: Irregular changes or variations in weather conditions, such as temperature or pressure.
words.example: The fluctuation of ocean temperatures influences the intensity of tropical storms.

words.definitionEn: The beginning or start of a season, weather event, or climatic condition.
words.example: The onset of the monsoon season brings heavy rains that are vital for agriculture.

words.definitionEn: The condition of the atmosphere at a particular place and time.
words.example: The weather in the mountains can change very quickly during the summer.

words.definitionEn: The star at the centre of our solar system that gives light and heat.
words.example: The sun rose over the hills, warming the frozen fields below.

words.definitionEn: A mass of tiny water droplets floating in the sky.
words.example: Dark clouds gathered over the bay, warning us of an approaching storm.

words.definitionEn: Air moving across the earth, especially when it moves quickly.
words.example: A cool wind blew from the sea, carrying the smell of salt.

words.definitionEn: White flakes of frozen water that fall from the sky in winter.
words.example: Heavy snow covered the village, closing the roads for several days.

words.definitionEn: A violent weather event with strong winds, heavy rain or snow.
words.example: A violent storm knocked down trees and cut power across the whole town.

words.definitionEn: How hot or cold the air, water or ground is, usually measured in degrees.
words.example: The temperature dropped sharply overnight, leaving the lake covered in ice.

words.definitionEn: Having a comfortable, moderately high temperature.
words.example: The afternoon was warm, so we swam in the lake until sunset.

words.definitionEn: Having a low temperature, or feeling chilly to the touch.
words.example: The cold morning air made our breath visible as we walked.

words.definitionEn: Having a high temperature, often uncomfortably so.
words.example: It was so hot that the asphalt on the road began to soften.

words.definitionEn: The warmest season of the year, between spring and autumn.
words.example: Many tourists visit the coast during summer to enjoy the long sunny days.

words.definitionEn: The coldest season of the year, between autumn and spring.
words.example: In winter, the mountain villages are often cut off by deep snow.

words.definitionEn: A curved band of colours in the sky caused by sunlight shining through rain.
words.example: A bright rainbow appeared after the shower, arching across the valley.

words.definitionEn: The loud rumbling sound that follows a flash of lightning.
words.example: Thunder rumbled in the distance, so we hurried indoors.

words.definitionEn: Water frozen into a solid state at or below zero degrees.
words.example: The children skated carefully across the ice on the frozen pond.

words.definitionEn: One of the four main periods of the year, each with its own weather.
words.example: Spring is my favourite season because flowers bloom everywhere.

words.definitionEn: Having little or no water or moisture in the air or ground.
words.example: The dry season lasts from November until May in this region.

words.definitionEn: Characterised by a lot of rain falling over a period of time.
words.example: Rainy days are common in autumn, so remember to bring an umbrella.

words.definitionEn: A gentle, light wind, often pleasant on a warm day.
words.example: A gentle breeze drifted through the open window, cooling the room.

words.definitionEn: Having a high amount of moisture in the air, making it feel damp.
words.example: The air was humid and heavy, so we walked slowly through the jungle.

words.definitionEn: A sudden strong rush of wind lasting only a short time.
words.example: A strong gust of wind tore the umbrella from her hands.

words.definitionEn: A sudden heavy fall of rain that lasts a short time.
words.example: A sudden downpour soaked the crowd before they could reach shelter.

words.definitionEn: Covered with cloud, so that the sky appears grey and dull.
words.example: The sky remained overcast all day, and no sunshine broke through.

words.meaningVi: mưa rào đột ngột, trút nước
words.definitionEn: A sudden very heavy rainstorm, often causing flash floods.
words.example: A cloudburst turned the dry riverbed into a rushing torrent within minutes.

words.definitionEn: Damage to skin and tissue caused by exposure to extreme cold.
words.example: Climbers wore thick gloves to prevent frostbite on their fingers.

words.definitionEn: Extremely hot, burning and intense.
words.example: The scorching midday sun drove everyone indoors until late afternoon.

words.definitionEn: Hot, humid and still, making the air feel heavy.
words.example: The sultry afternoon made even the lazy dogs lie motionless in the shade.

words.definitionEn: Warm, mild and pleasant, often used of evenings.
words.example: We sat outside on the balmy evening, listening to crickets in the garden.

words.definitionEn: Unpleasantly cold, in a way that makes one shiver.
words.example: A chilly wind swept across the empty beach in late October.

words.definitionEn: Extremely cold, often describing weather or air temperature.
words.example: The frigid air outside made the windows freeze over overnight.

words.definitionEn: Not severe or extreme, typically describing weather that is gentle.
words.example: This coastal town enjoys mild winters that rarely drop below freezing.

words.definitionEn: The force exerted by the weight of air on a given area.
words.example: Falling air pressure often signals that rain is approaching soon.

words.definitionEn: Direct light and warmth from the sun reaching the ground.
words.example: After days of rain, the sunshine finally broke through the clouds.

words.definitionEn: The total amount of rain that falls in a particular area over time.
words.example: Annual rainfall in the highlands has fallen steadily over the past decade.

words.definitionEn: A small ball of ice that falls from clouds during a storm.
words.example: Hailstones the size of marbles bounced off the car roof during the storm.

words.meaningVi: bão nhiệt đới Tây Thái Bình Dương
words.definitionEn: A tropical storm with very strong winds, found in the western Pacific.
words.example: The typhoon struck the coast overnight, flooding streets and damaging hundreds of homes.

words.definitionEn: A sudden, violent rush of wind, often with rain or snow.
words.example: A fierce squall blew in from the north, scattering boats across the harbour.

words.definitionEn: A type of white, fluffy cloud with flat bases and rounded tops.
words.example: Cumulus clouds drifted lazily across the blue sky above the fields.

words.definitionEn: A low, grey layer of cloud that covers the sky evenly.
words.example: A thick stratus layer hung over the city, blocking out all the sunlight.

words.definitionEn: Light rain made up of very fine, small drops.
words.example: A fine drizzle fell all morning, leaving the pavements slick and grey.

words.definitionEn: To turn into ice, or to become very cold when water hardens.
words.example: Water in the pipes can freeze overnight when temperatures drop below zero.

words.definitionEn: A line on a weather map joining points of equal atmospheric pressure.
words.example: Closely spaced isobars on the chart indicate a powerful wind forming over the sea.

words.definitionEn: The boundary between two air masses of different temperature and humidity.
words.example: A cold front approaching from the west will bring showers by evening.

words.definitionEn: The transfer of heat through the upward movement of warm air or fluid.
words.example: Convection currents in the atmosphere drive the formation of towering storm clouds.

words.definitionEn: The horizontal transport of heat or moisture by the movement of air masses.
words.example: Advection of warm, moist air from the ocean keeps the coastline unusually mild.

words.definitionEn: Energy emitted as waves, including the light and heat that come from the sun.
words.example: Solar radiation warms the surface of the earth, which then heats the air above it.

words.definitionEn: The proportion of incoming sunlight reflected by a surface such as ice or cloud.
words.example: Melting ice lowers albedo, so the darker ocean absorbs more heat and warms faster.

words.meaningVi: sự hạ xuống của không khí
words.definitionEn: The gradual downward movement of air that warms and dries as it descends.
words.example: Subsidence of dry air over the desert suppresses cloud formation and rainfall.

words.definitionEn: Irregular, rough movement of air that causes unsteady flight or rough weather.
words.example: Passengers were told to fasten their seatbelts because of severe turbulence over the mountains.

words.definitionEn: A spiral mass of air or water that spins rapidly around a central point.
words.example: A vortex of swirling air formed above the lake, lifting dust into the sky.

words.definitionEn: To cause something to happen suddenly, or to fall as rain or snow.
words.example: The rapidly cooling air mass may precipitate heavy snow across the northern plains.

words.definitionEn: The state in which air holds the maximum amount of water vapour possible.
words.example: When air reaches saturation, water vapour condenses into droplets to form clouds.

words.definitionEn: A towering dark cloud that produces thunderstorms, heavy rain and hail.
words.example: A huge cumulonimbus cloud towered over the plain before the storm broke.

words.definitionEn: A thick grey cloud layer that brings steady, continuous rain or snow.
words.example: A dense nimbostratus layer settled over the valley and brought steady rain all day.

words.definitionEn: Describing weather that is unpleasantly harsh, cold or stormy.
words.example: Inclement weather forced the organisers to postpone the outdoor festival until Sunday.

words.definitionEn: A large area of high pressure associated with settled, calm weather.
words.example: A persistent anticyclone brought days of clear skies and cold, still nights.

words.definitionEn: An elongated area of low pressure in the atmosphere.
words.example: A trough of low pressure moved slowly across the region, bringing unsettled showers.

words.definitionEn: A gentle, mild breeze, often blowing from the west.
words.example: A soft zephyr stirred the blossoms as we strolled through the orchard.

words.definitionEn: A severe flooding of land, often caused by heavy rain or storm surge.
words.example: Inundation of the lowlands destroyed crops and forced thousands of villagers to evacuate.

words.definitionEn: An extremely heavy fall of rain, or an overwhelming flood of water.
words.example: A deluge of rain fell on the city overnight, overwhelming the drainage system.

words.definitionEn: Describing rain that falls in an extremely heavy and violent way.
words.example: Torrential rain transformed the quiet street into a fast-flowing stream.

words.definitionEn: The condition of having very little rainfall and an extremely dry climate.
words.example: Rising aridity has shortened the growing season across much of the continent.

words.definitionEn: The amount of solar radiation received over an area during a given time.
words.example: Insolation on the south-facing slopes is far greater than on the shaded northern side.

words.definitionEn: An instrument used for measuring the moisture content of the air.
words.example: The technician checked the hygrometer to confirm the humidity inside the greenhouse.

words.definitionEn: An instrument that measures the speed of wind.
words.example: The anemometer on the rooftop recorded gusts of more than ninety kilometres an hour.

words.definitionEn: A line on a map connecting places that receive equal amounts of rainfall.
words.example: The isohyet map shows rainfall dropping sharply from the coast toward the interior.

words.definitionEn: A fast, narrow current of air high in the atmosphere that steers weather systems.
words.example: The jet stream shifted south this winter, bringing unusually cold air to the region.

words.definitionEn: A rotating thunderstorm with a deep, persistent updraft that can produce tornadoes.
words.example: Forecasters warned that a dangerous supercell was forming over the western plains.

words.meaningVi: tỷ suất giảm nhiệt theo độ cao
words.definitionEn: The rate at which air temperature decreases with increasing altitude.
words.example: A steep lapse rate encourages rising air currents that build tall storm clouds.

words.definitionEn: A natural light display in polar skies caused by charged particles from the sun.
words.example: Green curtains of the aurora shimmered across the northern sky all night.

words.definitionEn: An optical illusion caused by light bending through layers of hot air.
words.example: Travellers in the desert often mistake a shimmering mirage for a distant lake.

words.definitionEn: A thin layer of dust, smoke or moisture that reduces visibility in the air.
words.example: A thick haze of smoke from distant fires hung over the valley for days.

words.meaningVi: xoáy nước dữ dội, cơn lốc
words.definitionEn: A violent whirlpool or turbulent situation, often in the sea or air.
words.example: The fishing boat was caught in a maelstrom of waves and howling wind.

words.definitionEn: Describing a warm period between two ice ages.
words.example: Scientists study ancient ice cores to understand past interglacial periods on Earth.

words.definitionEn: A form of oxygen in the upper atmosphere that absorbs harmful ultraviolet radiation.
words.example: Chemicals released on the ground have thinned the ozone layer over the poles.

words.definitionEn: The pleasant earthy smell produced when rain falls on dry ground.
words.example: The petrichor rising from the parched garden was the first sign of relief.

words.meaningVi: ống thuỷ tinh do sét đánh
words.definitionEn: A tube of glassy rock formed when lightning strikes sand or soil.
words.example: Hikers discovered a fulgurite in the dunes, formed by a lightning strike centuries ago.

words.definitionEn: The soft light of dusk or dawn, when the sun is just below the horizon.
words.example: The crepuscule painted the lake in soft violet hues before the stars appeared.

words.definitionEn: A hot, dusty wind blowing north from the Sahara into southern Europe.
words.example: A sirocco swept across Sicily, coating cars and balconies with fine red dust.

words.definitionEn: A warm, dry wind that descends the leeward side of a mountain range.
words.example: A foehn wind raised temperatures sharply in the Alpine valley after the snow melted.

words.definitionEn: A warm, dry wind that descends the eastern slopes of the Rockies.
words.example: A chinook melted the snow across the prairies in a single afternoon.

words.definitionEn: A cold, violent wind that blows down from mountains toward the Adriatic Sea.
words.example: The bora gusted fiercely along the Croatian coast, rattling shutters and tossing boats.

words.definitionEn: A cold, strong northwesterly wind that blows through southern France.
words.example: The mistral swept through Provence, bending the cypress trees and cooling the vineyards.

words.definitionEn: A violent dust storm produced when thunderstorm outflow lifts sand into the air.
words.example: A towering haboob rolled across the desert, plunging the town into brown darkness.

words.definitionEn: Soft, snow-like ice pellets formed when supercooled droplets freeze onto snowflakes.
words.example: Graupel bounced off the windscreen, forming a crunchy white layer on the road.

words.definitionEn: A white, granular coating of ice that forms on objects in freezing fog.
words.example: Rime coated every branch and fence post along the mountain path that morning.

words.definitionEn: Feathery crystals of ice that form on surfaces on clear, cold nights.
words.example: Hoarfrost sparkled on the meadow grass as the sun rose over the frozen valley.

words.definitionEn: A thin, transparent coating of ice on roads, rocks or pavements.
words.example: Verglas formed overnight on the mountain road, making driving extremely treacherous.

words.definitionEn: A powerful storm moving northeast along the Atlantic coast of North America.
words.example: A powerful nor'easter battered the coast, flooding roads and knocking out power lines.

words.definitionEn: A hot, dry foehn-like wind on the eastern side of the Andes.
words.example: Zonda winds carried dust across Mendoza, leaving the vineyards coated in grit.

words.meaningVi: gió giật đột ngột trên vịnh
words.definitionEn: A sudden violent gust of wind blowing down from mountains onto water.
words.example: A williwaw struck the anchored yacht without warning, snapping its mooring lines.

words.definitionEn: A small, swirling column of dust and air rising from hot ground.
words.example: A dust devil spun across the empty car park, lifting leaves and paper.

words.definitionEn: A rotating column of air and water spray over the sea or a lake.
words.example: Tourists watched a waterspout twist across the bay before it dissipated.

words.definitionEn: A widespread, long-lived windstorm associated with a line of severe thunderstorms.
words.example: The derecho flattened thousands of trees across several states in a single night.

words.definitionEn: Stormy, turbulent or violently emotional.
words.example: The tempestuous sea hurled waves against the cliffs throughout the long night.

words.definitionEn: Characterised by strong, gusty wind that blows in bursts.
words.example: A blustery afternoon sent leaves swirling across the cobbled square.

words.definitionEn: Characterised by sudden squalls of wind, often accompanied by rain.
words.example: Squally showers swept across the harbour, forcing the ferries to stay in port.

words.definitionEn: Relating to winter, especially its cold and dormant character.
words.example: The brumal landscape lay silent under a thick blanket of snow.

words.definitionEn: Relating to or characteristic of the summer season.
words.example: Estival heat built slowly over the plains until the afternoon grew unbearable.

words.definitionEn: Relating to spring, or appearing during the spring season.
words.example: Vernal rains brought fresh green shoots to the parched hillsides after winter.

words.definitionEn: Relating to autumn, especially its mild, golden or cool character.
words.example: The autumnal light turned the maple forest into a glowing tapestry of gold.

words.definitionEn: The extent or density of cloud cover across the sky.
words.example: Increasing nebulosity over the mountains suggested that rain would arrive before dawn.

words.definitionEn: Wispy, feathery high-altitude clouds made of ice crystals.
words.example: Thin cirrus clouds streaked the sky, foretelling a change in the weather.

words.definitionEn: A thin, sheet-like layer of high ice cloud often creating halos.
words.example: Cirrostratus clouds veiled the sun, creating a faint halo around its disc.

words.definitionEn: Mid-level white or grey cloud in rounded patches or rolls.
words.example: Altocumulus clouds rolled across the sky like a sea of white pebbles at dusk.

words.definitionEn: Low, ragged clouds driven rapidly by strong wind.
words.example: Scud raced across the grey sky, driven by a fierce wind from the sea.

words.definitionEn: Streaks of precipitation falling from a cloud that evaporate before reaching the ground.
words.example: Dark virga hung beneath the clouds, but no rain reached the thirsty dry fields.

words.definitionEn: Pouch-like clouds hanging beneath the base of a storm cloud.
words.example: Mammatus clouds hung ominously beneath the anvil, signalling a severe storm.

words.definitionEn: Lens-shaped, describing clouds that form over mountains in stable air.
words.example: Lenticular clouds hovered motionless above the peak, like stacked silver plates.

words.definitionEn: A faint, white arc of light appearing in fog opposite the sun.
words.example: A pale fogbow curved across the mist above the frozen lake at sunrise.

words.definitionEn: A bright spot of light beside the sun, caused by refraction through ice crystals.
words.example: Observers saw a bright parhelion beside the sun, a rare halo of refracted light.
