words.definitionEn: To make something as effective, efficient, or functional as possible, often using algorithms.
words.example: Engineers use machine learning to optimise the energy consumption of data centres.

words.meaningVi: dựa trên dữ liệu, lấy dữ liệu làm nền tảng
words.definitionEn: Guided or determined by data analysis rather than intuition or experience alone.
words.example: A data-driven approach to policy-making can lead to more accurate predictions of social outcomes.

words.meaningVi: sự công bằng, tính công bằng
words.definitionEn: The quality of treating people equally and without bias, a key concern in AI ethics.
words.example: Ensuring fairness in AI systems requires careful testing for hidden biases in training data.

words.meaningVi: bước đột phá, thành tựu quan trọng
words.definitionEn: A sudden, significant advance or discovery, especially in science or technology.
words.example: The breakthrough in natural language processing allowed machines to understand context much better than before.

words.meaningVi: khả năng thích nghi, tính linh hoạt
words.definitionEn: The capacity to adjust to new conditions or changes in the environment, a valuable trait for AI systems.
words.example: The adaptability of reinforcement learning agents makes them suitable for dynamic environments like stock trading.

words.definitionEn: To come together from different directions to form a single point or common goal, used in technology and AI.
words.example: As AI and biotechnology converge, new possibilities for personalised medicine are emerging.

words.meaningVi: phương pháp heuristic, phỏng đoán có hệ thống
words.definitionEn: A problem-solving approach that uses a practical method not guaranteed to be optimal but sufficient for immediate goals.
words.example: A common heuristic in AI pathfinding is to estimate the distance to the target using a straight-line formula.

words.definitionEn: A typical example or pattern of something, especially a set of ideas that form a framework for thinking.
words.example: The shift from rule-based programming to deep learning represents a major paradigm change in AI research.

words.definitionEn: The combination of separate elements or ideas to form a coherent whole, often in AI system design.
words.example: The synthesis of vision and language models has enabled more advanced image captioning systems.

words.definitionEn: An electronic machine that stores and processes information following instructions.
words.example: My grandfather learned to use a computer when he was seventy.

words.definitionEn: A machine that can carry out tasks automatically, often controlled by a computer.
words.example: The factory uses a robot to pack boxes faster than people can.

words.definitionEn: A worldwide network of computers that allows people to share information.
words.example: Most students now use the internet to research their homework.

words.definitionEn: Facts and figures collected and stored so they can be analysed or used.
words.example: The company stores customer data on secure servers in the city.

words.definitionEn: A software program designed to run on a phone or tablet for a specific purpose.
words.example: I downloaded a translation app before my trip to Japan.

words.definitionEn: A mobile phone that can run apps, access the internet and take photos.
words.example: Almost everyone in our office now carries a smartphone everywhere.

words.definitionEn: The flat surface of a device on which images and text are displayed.
words.example: Staring at a screen for hours can make your eyes feel tired.

words.definitionEn: A device with moving parts that performs a task, often using power.
words.example: The new machine can sort thousands of parcels in a single hour.

words.definitionEn: Programs and instructions that tell a computer what to do.
words.example: The school installed new software to help teachers track homework.

words.definitionEn: A set of linked pages on the internet, owned by a person or organisation.
words.example: You can book your train tickets through the company's website.

words.definitionEn: A system of connected computers, devices or people that share information.
words.example: The office network went down, so nobody could send emails.

words.definitionEn: A device that stores electrical energy and supplies power to a machine.
words.example: The electric car's battery can travel more than four hundred kilometres.

words.definitionEn: The time that is yet to come, or the period after the present moment.
words.example: Many experts believe that robots will change the future of work.

words.definitionEn: To create something new that did not exist before, such as a device or method.
words.example: Scientists invented a machine that can sort recycling automatically.

words.definitionEn: To plan and create the form or structure of something before making it.
words.example: Engineers designed the robot to walk up stairs safely.

words.definitionEn: To operate a machine or system, or to make it behave in a certain way.
words.example: A single engineer can control the whole fleet of drones from a tablet.

words.definitionEn: The paid work that a person does regularly to earn money.
words.example: Some people worry that machines will take away their job.

words.definitionEn: To gain knowledge or skill, often by study, practice or experience.
words.example: The program can learn from millions of photos without help.

words.definitionEn: To teach a system or person a skill by giving them examples and practice.
words.example: Engineers train the model on thousands of medical scans.

words.definitionEn: A situation that is difficult to deal with or needs a solution.
words.example: The team fixed a serious problem in the software before launch.

words.definitionEn: A way of solving a problem or dealing with a difficult situation.
words.example: The startup offers a simple solution for managing energy use at home.

words.definitionEn: A device that detects changes in light, heat, motion or pressure and reports them.
words.example: A motion sensor switches on the lights when someone enters the room.

words.definitionEn: Written instructions in a programming language that tell a computer what to do.
words.example: The engineer rewrote the code to make the app run much faster.

words.definitionEn: A small piece of silicon carrying electronic circuits that process information.
words.example: The new phone uses a faster chip that saves battery power.

words.definitionEn: The physical parts of a computer or electronic device that you can touch.
words.example: Upgrading the hardware will allow the system to handle more users.

words.definitionEn: Existing or done on a computer or the internet rather than in the physical world.
words.example: Students attended a virtual classroom from their homes across the country.

words.definitionEn: Working by itself without needing a person to operate or control it.
words.example: The doors are automatic, so they open as you approach them.

words.definitionEn: A small useful device or tool, often electronic and new.
words.example: He loves buying the latest gadget as soon as it appears in shops.

words.definitionEn: To copy a file or program from the internet onto your own device.
words.example: I downloaded the update so the phone would have better security.

words.definitionEn: To send a file or data from your device to a website or server.
words.example: She uploaded her research photos to the shared project folder.

words.definitionEn: To gain unauthorised access to a computer system, often to steal or damage data.
words.example: Criminals tried to hack the bank's website to steal customer details.

words.definitionEn: To convert information into a coded form so that only authorised people can read it.
words.example: The messaging app encrypts every message before it leaves your phone.

words.definitionEn: The right to keep personal information and private life away from others.
words.example: Many people worry about privacy when using smart home devices.

words.definitionEn: The practice of protecting computers, networks and data from digital attacks.
words.example: The bank invested heavily in cybersecurity after the attack last year.

words.definitionEn: A small aircraft flown without a pilot on board, controlled remotely.
words.example: A delivery drone dropped the parcel in the garden within minutes.

words.definitionEn: An early model of a product built to test ideas before full production.
words.example: The team showed a working prototype of the robot to investors.

words.definitionEn: A newly founded company, often built around a fresh technology or idea.
words.example: The young startup aims to build affordable drones for farmers.

words.definitionEn: A system or service on which software, content or businesses are built and run.
words.example: The learning platform lets teachers share lessons with students online.

words.definitionEn: The point or means through which a user interacts with a computer or system.
words.example: The new interface is simpler, so older users can find features quickly.

words.definitionEn: Designed to be worn on the body, such as a watch that tracks health.
words.example: A wearable device counted my steps and monitored my heart rate.

words.definitionEn: An official rule made by an authority to control how something is done.
words.example: New regulation requires AI firms to explain how their systems decide.

words.definitionEn: An advantage or helpful result that something provides to people.
words.example: One clear benefit of automation is that workers avoid dangerous tasks.

words.definitionEn: The possibility that something harmful or unpleasant might happen.
words.example: There is a real risk that the system could make unfair decisions.

words.definitionEn: A person or company that pays people to work for them.
words.example: Many employers now expect staff to learn basic coding skills.

words.definitionEn: The series of jobs and professional progress a person makes during their working life.
words.example: She changed her career from teaching to data analysis last year.

words.definitionEn: To examine something quickly with a device, or to copy it digitally.
words.example: The software can scan thousands of documents for errors in minutes.

words.definitionEn: The ability of a machine or system to operate independently without human control.
words.example: The debate centres on how much autonomy self-driving cars should have.

words.definitionEn: Highly developed, complex and advanced in design or understanding.
words.example: The lab uses sophisticated sensors to monitor air quality in real time.

words.definitionEn: Able to grow or expand to handle a larger amount of work or users.
words.example: The platform is scalable, so it can serve millions of users at once.

words.meaningVi: lỗi thời, không còn dùng được
words.definitionEn: No longer used or useful because something newer has replaced it.
words.example: Many traditional skills may become obsolete within a few decades.

words.definitionEn: To increase rapidly in number or spread widely over a short period.
words.example: Chatbots have proliferated across websites in just a few years.

words.definitionEn: Spreading gradually to affect every part of something or every aspect of life.
words.example: Algorithms have become pervasive in shopping, news and entertainment.

words.definitionEn: To make something bad less severe or less harmful.
words.example: Engineers aim to mitigate the risks of failure with extra safety checks.

words.definitionEn: To examine something very carefully in order to find faults or important details.
words.example: Regulators scrutinise the software before it is allowed on the market.

words.definitionEn: The obligation to explain and take responsibility for what a system or person does.
words.example: Accountability is hard to establish when an algorithm makes a mistake.

words.definitionEn: The quality of being open about how decisions and processes actually work.
words.example: Users demand transparency about how the app chooses what they see.

words.definitionEn: A proposed explanation that can be tested by observation or experiment.
words.example: The researchers tested their hypothesis using a large set of images.

words.definitionEn: Based on observation, experiment or evidence rather than on theory alone.
words.example: Empirical tests showed the model performed well only on familiar data.

words.definitionEn: To measure or express something as an exact amount or number.
words.example: It is difficult to quantify the value of creativity in a machine.

words.meaningVi: triển khai, đưa vào sử dụng
words.definitionEn: To bring a system, tool or force into use in a planned and organised way.
words.example: The city will deploy autonomous buses on three main routes next year.

words.definitionEn: The basic physical and organisational systems needed for a society to function.
words.example: Reliable internet infrastructure is essential for remote learning programmes.

words.definitionEn: The system of rules and processes by which an organisation or state is managed.
words.example: Strong governance is needed to control how powerful AI tools are used.

words.meaningVi: hệ quả, tác động kéo theo
words.definitionEn: A consequence or complex outcome that follows from an action or decision.
words.example: The ramifications of replacing workers with robots extend far beyond the factory.

words.definitionEn: A statement or situation that seems contradictory but may still be true.
words.example: It is a paradox that the most connected age is also the most isolated.

words.meaningVi: mang tính loạn lạc, phản địa đàng
words.definitionEn: Describing an imagined society where life is extremely bad, controlled or oppressive.
words.example: The dystopian novel imagines a city where every move is watched by machines.

words.definitionEn: To form opinions or guesses about something without having complete evidence.
words.example: Experts speculate about how jobs will look in the next twenty years.

words.definitionEn: Possible to do or achieve in a practical way, with available resources.
words.example: Building a fully automated city within five years is not feasible.

words.meaningVi: khả thi, có thể tồn tại
words.definitionEn: Capable of working successfully or surviving, especially as a business plan.
words.example: The startup proved that its model was viable after its first year.

words.definitionEn: Dealing with situations sensibly and practically rather than by fixed theory.
words.example: Her pragmatic approach focused on what the team could actually deliver.

words.definitionEn: Depending on certain conditions or circumstances that may or may not happen.
words.example: The funding is contingent on the success of the first trial.

words.definitionEn: Just beginning to develop and not yet fully formed or established.
words.example: The nascent field of quantum computing attracts many young researchers.

words.definitionEn: Happening in small, gradual steps rather than through one big change.
words.example: Incremental updates to the software improved its speed each month.

words.definitionEn: Able to work together with other systems or devices without special effort.
words.example: The hospital chose interoperable software so records could be shared easily.

words.meaningVi: tiêu chuẩn so sánh, điểm chuẩn
words.definitionEn: A standard or reference point used to measure and compare performance.
words.example: The new model set a benchmark for accuracy in image recognition.

words.definitionEn: A system or process by which something works or achieves a result.
words.example: The mechanism that adjusts the robot's balance is surprisingly simple.

words.definitionEn: The ability or power to do something, especially a task or function.
words.example: New capability in image analysis helps doctors spot early signs of disease.

words.definitionEn: The process of becoming outdated or no longer needed, often because of new technology.
words.example: Planned obsolescence forces people to replace their phones every few years.

words.meaningVi: có tri giác, có cảm giác
words.definitionEn: Able to perceive or feel things through the senses, as living beings do.
words.example: Whether a future machine could be sentient remains a hotly debated question.

words.definitionEn: Having human shape or human characteristics, especially when applied to machines or animals.
words.example: The anthropomorphic robot has a face and expressive eyes like a person.

words.definitionEn: Impossible to avoid, resist or escape, such as an inevitable outcome.
words.example: Many thinkers believe that technological change is ineluctable and unstoppable.

words.definitionEn: Impossible to stop or prevent, continuing steadily despite all efforts.
words.example: The inexorable rise of automation is changing every industry on Earth.

words.definitionEn: Representing the most perfect or typical example of a particular quality.
words.example: The lab is the quintessential picture of a modern research centre.

words.definitionEn: The branch of philosophy that studies knowledge, how it is acquired and its limits.
words.example: Epistemology asks whether a machine can truly know anything at all.

words.definitionEn: The philosophical study of what kinds of things exist and their basic nature.
words.example: Ontology questions whether artificial minds should count as real beings.

words.definitionEn: The explanation of things in terms of their purpose or intended goal.
words.example: Some critics see the design of intelligent systems as a form of teleology.

words.definitionEn: A remedy believed to cure all problems or difficulties at once.
words.example: Many people treat artificial intelligence as a panacea for every social problem.

words.definitionEn: An illusion or unrealistic hope that is impossible to achieve in practice.
words.example: Fully error-free software is often a chimera that developers chase in vain.

words.definitionEn: Excessive pride or self-confidence that often leads to a downfall.
words.example: The company's hubris led it to ignore warnings about the flawed system.

words.definitionEn: A person who opposes new technology, especially new machines or methods.
words.example: Calling every critic a luddite ignores their real concerns about privacy.

words.meaningVi: chế độ trị vì của giới kỹ trị
words.definitionEn: A system of government in which experts and technical specialists hold the power.
words.example: Critics warn that a technocracy may place decisions beyond ordinary citizens.

words.meaningVi: sự thống trị, ưu thế vượt trội
words.definitionEn: A position of dominance or greater power over others, gained over time.
words.example: The rapid ascendancy of chatbots surprised many traditional software firms.

words.definitionEn: Awareness or knowledge of something, especially as it affects a situation.
words.example: The board took cognisance of the risks before approving the new system.

words.definitionEn: A division into two sharply contrasting parts or opposing ideas.
words.example: There is a dichotomy between the promise of AI and the fear it inspires.

words.definitionEn: A change of circumstances, especially one that is unexpected or unpleasant.
words.example: The firm survived many vicissitudes before becoming a leader in robotics.

words.meaningVi: lực lượng khổng lồ không thể cản
words.definitionEn: A huge, powerful force or organisation that cannot easily be stopped.
words.example: The tech giant became a juggernaut that dominated the entire online market.

words.meaningVi: tận thế, mang tính hủy diệt
words.definitionEn: Describing a scene of great destruction or the end of the world.
words.example: Some films paint an apocalyptic picture of machines ruling the planet.

words.meaningVi: bao quát, giám sát toàn diện
words.definitionEn: Allowing a full view of everything at once, often used of surveillance systems.
words.example: The city's panoptic cameras watch every street corner without rest.

words.definitionEn: Relating to or caused by motion, especially the energy that a moving object has.
words.example: The robot converts kinetic energy from its moving arm into stored power.

words.definitionEn: Vague, unclear or not yet clearly formed, lacking definite shape or detail.
words.example: The plan for the new AI policy remains nebulous and poorly defined.

words.definitionEn: Remaining in a reduced form after its original purpose has largely disappeared.
words.example: Some old office habits feel vestigial now that software handles the work.

words.definitionEn: Stubbornly resisting authority, control or attempts to make one change.
words.example: The recalcitrant software kept crashing despite every update the team made.

words.definitionEn: To remove a need or problem by taking action in advance.
words.example: Automatic backups obviate the need for manual copying of every file.

words.definitionEn: A regular rhythm or pattern of sound or movement, often in speech or music.
words.example: The synthetic voice imitated the natural cadence of a human storyteller.

words.definitionEn: Understood only by a few people with specialised or secret knowledge.
words.example: The arcane mathematics behind the model baffled most of the audience.

words.meaningVi: khó hiểu, chỉ dành cho số ít người
words.definitionEn: Intended for or understood by only a small group with special knowledge.
words.example: The esoteric research papers are read by only a handful of specialists.

words.meaningVi: gây phiền toái, gây bực bội
words.definitionEn: Causing annoyance or worry, often by being unnecessary or troublesome.
words.example: The vexatious bugs delayed the launch for several frustrating weeks.

words.definitionEn: Sparkling brilliantly, or very lively, witty and clever in conversation.
words.example: The scintillating presentation dazzled the audience with new ideas.

words.meaningVi: không thể diễn tả bằng lời
words.definitionEn: Too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words.
words.example: The beauty of a well-written algorithm can feel almost ineffable to its creators.

words.definitionEn: Beginning to happen or develop, but not yet fully apparent.
words.example: Researchers noticed incipient signs of bias in the early test results.

words.definitionEn: Showing great care, persistence and diligence in one's work over time.
words.example: The sedulous engineers tested every line of code before the release.

words.definitionEn: Something placed in the wrong historical period, or something outdated now.
words.example: Paper ledgers in a modern bank are an anachronism that surprised visitors.

words.definitionEn: The quality of appearing to be real or true, especially in fiction or simulation.
words.example: The film's verisimilitude makes the imagined future feel frighteningly real.

words.definitionEn: A particular mode or form in which something is experienced or expressed.
words.example: The assistant combines several input modality types, including voice and images.

words.definitionEn: Having a keen insight and a clear understanding of complex situations.
words.example: The perspicacious analyst spotted the flaw in the model at once.

words.definitionEn: A gap or missing part, especially in a text, record or body of knowledge.
words.example: The study revealed a serious lacuna in the data about older users.

words.meaningVi: chủ nghĩa cải thiện thế giới
words.definitionEn: The belief that the world can be improved through human effort and progress.
words.example: Her meliorism led her to believe that technology could solve many social problems.

words.meaningVi: người canh gác, hệ thống canh gác
words.definitionEn: A guard or watchful device that keeps close observation over something.
words.example: The monitoring system acts as a sentinel, alerting staff to any intrusion.

words.meaningVi: ghi nhớ bằng mẹo, gợi nhớ
words.definitionEn: A device such as a rhyme or pattern that helps people remember information.
words.example: The engineer used a mnemonic to recall the steps of the startup process.

words.definitionEn: Clear and easy to understand, or transparent and very clear in appearance.
words.example: The professor's pellucid explanation made the algorithm easy to grasp.

words.definitionEn: Approaching a limit or value more and more closely but never quite reaching it.
words.example: The error rate falls in an asymptotic curve as the training data grows.
